articleTitle: Design and simulation of C-band bifrequency Magnetically Insulated transmission Line Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A novel idea of azimuthal partition to generate high power microwave with two frequencies (named bifrequency) in a single device is put forward for the first time in this paper. According to this idea, resorting to azimuthal partition of cavity-depth in a conventional Magnetically Insulated transmission Line Oscillator (MILO), a C-band bifrequency MILO (BFMILO) is designed and simulated. The analysis of BFMILO shows that the operation in BFMILO is in particular partition. The results of particle simulation are presented: Employing an electron beam of 490 kV and 45kA, a C-band BFMILO can generate about 1.43GW of high power microwave with two frequencies. They are respectively 3.4 GHz and 3.65 GHz. The power efficiency is about 6.5%. The amplitude difference of the spectrum between the two frequencies is about 0.4 dB.

articleTitle: Designing and testing of high-coupling Tesla transformer
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: One of the most widely applied devices for repetitive pulse power generator is high-coupling Tesla transformer. The general designing of the high-coupling Tesla transformer is described in this paper. Because of the requirement of high coupling for Tesla transformer, an open-loop magnetic core is employed. In order to reach high reliability of this high-voltage generator, the windings of Tesla transformer (both primary winding and second winding) are set compactly within the insulating gap of pulse forming line (PFL). The parameters of primary and secondary loops have be well-connectedly designed and suitably adjusted. Moreover, as one of the most important components of the TPG700, a high-coupling Tesla transformer, with open-loop magnetic core applied in it, achieved a high efficiency about 83% after optimization. This Tesla transformer can operate on the range of repetition frequency from 1 to 100 Hz.

articleTitle: A repetitive high-current pulsed accelerator—TPG700
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The design and construction of a repetitive high-current pulsed accelerator-TPG700 is described in this paper. The accelerator consists of a Tesla transformer with 40 ohm build-in coaxial pulse forming line. The triggered high-pressure switch of TPG700 has the capability of conducting current of 17.5kA in 35ns' duration at 100 pps. The transformer was designed to operate at 1.4MV, when its primary capacitors were charged to approximately 1000V. Under the working state of 100pps, the jitter of breakdown of the switch voltages is lower than 1% on average. To enhance the overall efficiency of the pulser, resonant charging technology based on IGBTs was utilized. As the experimental results indicate, the total efficiency of the pulser, when measured on matched dummy load, is close to 75%. The experimental results indicate that in matching case, the output of 700kV, 17kA for 40Ω resistive load is obtained. Moreover, some experiments such as long lifetime cathode testing and high power microwave (HPM) generation using backward oscillator (BWO) have been conducted on TPG700.

articleTitle: Application of the coupled wave theory on design of HPM transmission line
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Over-mode circular waveguide is widely used to high power microwave transmission. The bend and conversion between modes of transmission line is required in many applications. In this paper, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode waveguide bends with different angle is designed by means of theoretical analyses of coupled wave and the constant curvature bend to give out relation between the bend angle and curvature radius of curved waveguide. Simultaneously the twin bend method is used to realize high efficiency conversion from TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode. The correctness of theoretical analysis of coupled wave is verified by numerical simulation in the design example.

articleTitle: CHIPIC: A highly efficient code for electromagnetic PIC modeling and simulation
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation is the most popular computational modeling of the interaction between charged particles and electromagnetic fields. Lots of PIC codes are written for simulating a wide range of challenging problems, including plasma physics, high power microwave devices, high power lasers, particle accelerators, and so forth. In this research, we design a highly efficient electromagnetic PIC code, called CHIPIC, which is applicable to almost all these problems. This code includes a computer aided design (CAD) system and a physical kernel. Considering the various complex physical models and numerical conditions in PIC simulation, the whole CAD system is divided into six functional modules and three system layers with object-oriented method, of which the six functional modules are basic setting, algorithmic setting, structural modeling, diagnostic setting, simulation control and data processing, and the system layers are user interface layer, data managing layer and computing interface layer. The physical kernel contains a mesh generator, two field solvers, a particle handler, an object manager and a data manager. It provides various algorithms and models to represent structural geometries, material properties, incoming and outgoing waves, particle emission processes and boundary conditions. In addition, powerful filter for numerical noise are also provided. This physical kernel can run on a single processor or in parallel mode. When it runs in parallel mode, the message pass interface (MPI) and open specifications for multiprocessing (OpenMP) is needed. At last, the validity of this electromagnetic PIC code is proved by simulating a magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator (MILO) tube.

articleTitle: A W-band gyrotron travelling wave amplifier using a helically corrugated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A gyrotron traveling wave amplifier (gyro-TWA) with a cusp electron gun and a helically corrugated waveguide operating in the W-band is presented. The large orbit electron beam from the cusp gun interacts resonantly with an ideal eigenwave existing in the interaction region based on the cyclotron resonance maser instability. When driven by the electron beam of energy 40 keV and current 1.5 A, the amplifier was simulated to output 10 kW (CW) with a 3 dB frequency bandwidth of 90-100 GHz and saturated gain of 40 dB. Linear analysis and numerical simulations of the performance characteristics of the amplifier will be presented.

articleTitle: An introduction to Mini-LIA
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Mini-LIA is a miniature of linear induction accelerator developed by China Academy of Engineering Physics and Tsinghua University. Double-pulsed beam emitting was realized with thermionic cathode and metglas core in induction accelerating cavity. Electron beam current more than 1.1A was obtained on condition of 80kV double-pulsed high voltage produced by pulsed power system supplying to injector and accelerating modules. Further improvement is under way.

articleTitle: Recent advances in radiographic X-ray source development at Sandia
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Recent experiments at Sandia National Laboratories have demonstrated electron beam diode X-ray sources capable of producing > 350 rad@m with 1.7mm FWHM x-ray source distributions, and endpoint energy spectrum in the 6–7 MeV range. A review of our present theoretical understanding of the diode(s) operation and our experimental and simulation methods to investigate them will be presented. Emphasis is given to e-beam sources used on state-of-the-art Induction Voltage Adder (IVA) pulsed-power accelerators. In addition, a brief discussion of a proposed radiographic system based on Linear Transformer Driver (LTD) technology is discussed.

articleTitle: Experimental studies on a repetitive pulsed power modulator with a compact Tesla transformer
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Experimental studies on a designed pulsed power modulator with a compact Tesla transformer in single and repetitive modes from low voltages to high voltages are experimentally carried out in turn. The experimental results are presented and analyzed. The conclusions are shown as follows: (1) the modulator's highest output voltage across a 100 Ω resistive load in single mode is obtained to be 330 kV with 7 ns pulse duration and 2 ns rise-time; (2) the cooling system and gas blowing system are unnecessary and not adopted experimentally in repetitive mode in the case that the number of pulses in a batch is less than or equal to 300, as a result, the volume and weight of the modulator system is reduced; (3) in the range of 300 pulses in a batch, with the increase of the number of pulses in repetitive mode, the average value of the output voltage declines and the pulse-to-pulse instability of the output voltage decreases, at the same time, the decline degree of the output voltage increases and reaches to be stable when the number of pulses in a batch is more than 50; (4) with the increase of the repetition rate, the pulse-to-pulse instability of the output voltage increases, and the average value of the output voltage declines, especially after the repetition rate exceeds 40 Hz; (5) pressurization can significantly improve the characteristics in repetitive mode and the improved level of the characteristics is almost the same for different pressurization level; (6) the pulsed power modulator can steadily output 310 kV for 300 pulses in 40 Hz repetition rate.

articleTitle: Particle simulation of X-band dual frequency coaxial relativistic backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: X-band dual frequency coaxial relativistic backward wave oscillator is suggested. The properties of dual frequency RBWO are investigated and optimized with electromagnetic simulation method. The results shown that steady dual frequencies microwave power outputs are generated with the operating voltage 590KV, beam current 9.4KA and the external guiding magnetic 0.7T. The microwave frequencies are 9.367GHz and 9.717GHz respectively with frequency differences 350MHz. The averaged output power is 0.75GW with efficiency 13.5%. The power amplitude difference is about 0.14dB.

articleTitle: Factors influencing one stage magnetic pulse compression system output
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A magnetic pulse compression system is presented which does not contain external remagnetization circuits that are commonly used in magnetic compressors. A one stage compressor suffices to form 20kV, ~70ns pulses across a 207Ω resistive load. Equivalent circuits for two consecutive operation stages of the compressor accounting for nonlinear processes in magnetic switches are described and analyzed thoroughly. In conclusion, to get higher amplitude and faster fall time voltage pulse on resistive load we need higher resistivity load, lower saturated inductance and faster switching time of magnetic switch.

articleTitle: Design of an energy recovery system for a Gyrotron backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: To realize the full potential of a Gyrotron backward wave oscillator (Gyro-BWO), an energy recovery system was designed using Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulations and optimized using both a Genetic Algorithm and PIC simulations. Simulations were carried out to optimize a periodic structure for separation of the spent electron beam and the output radiation produced by a gyro-BWO in the 8.0 - 9.5GHz frequency range. The spent electron beam can be collected using a multi-stage depressed collector. The number and electric potentials of the electrodes were optimized to achieve the best overall recovery efficiency for specific parameters of the spent beam. The 3D PIC code MAGIC was used to simulate electrons' trajectories and a Genetic Algorithm was used to refine the electrode shapes for optimum efficiency.

articleTitle: Beam characterizations of the Mini-LIA
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A miniature electron linear induction accelerator (Mini-LIA) is designed and constructed at Tsinghua University under the CAEP/Tsinghua collaboration. In this paper we present the beam characterizations for the Mini-LIA. The beam current is measured with a Faraday cup. The transverse beam profile is measured with a YAG screen. The beam energy is determined by observing the beam rotation angle in a solenoid, and the projected rms emittance is measured with the pepper-pot device.

articleTitle: Parallel electromagnetic FDTD program design and implementation on JASMIN
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A Parallel Electromagnetic FDTD (Finite Difference - Time Domain) program is designed and implemented on JASMIN (J parallel Adaptive Structured Mesh applications INfrastructure), which is developed by Beijing Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics. By means of encapsulating high performance data structure, integrating numerical methods, masking the parallelization and adaptive meshing technology, JASMIN accelerates the development of parallel programs which can employ modern HPC (High Performance Computer) efficiently. This parallel FDTD program is full-functional with FDTD iteration, excitation, UPML (Un-split Perfect Matched Layer) absorption boundary condition, automatic load balance, etc., and is verified by computing the radiation fields of an electric dipole. As an example, the near fields of a Gaussian beam focused by a spherical lens are simulated.

articleTitle: A compact,repetitive trigger generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This paper describes an innovative design of compact trigger generator with repetitive pulse to drive high voltage gas switch. The basic circuit of trigger generator is analyzed by using P-Spice software. The trigger generator consists of a charging capacitor, a pulse transformer, a trigger gas switch and a control circuit. The incorporate design of capacitor and transformer enables the generator to be compact, and the employing of IGBT switch makes the generator be operated stably. The output voltage of generator is up to 100KV at a pulse repetition rate of range 1Hz to 100Hz, and the during time of pulse is 1µs with a risetime of 500ns.

articleTitle: DC emitting characteristics of a single crystal LaB6 thermionic cathode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A diode-type electron gun is used to investigate the DC emitting characteristics of a single crystal LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> thermionic cathode. The emitting area is a planar 2-mm-diameter, achieving transmitted currents up to 175 mA and the current density 5.57A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Comparing the measured current with Longo equation, which is accurate and applicable in the regime of practical operation. The circumstance has an effect on the emitting ability of cathode, when the vacuum is more than 7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> Pa, and the current density apparently becomes lower. Aggradation and diffusion of LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> to pyrolytic graphite make the resistance of the heater lower. Experimental results show that DC emitting current density is lower than pulsed emitting due to the finite diffusion velocity of atom La and the surface adsorption of remainder-gas.

articleTitle: Low-energy, high-current electron beam transportation through a plasma channel in a guide magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The process of high-current, low-energy electron beam transportation through a plasma channel in a guide magnetic field has been studied experimentally and by the use of computer simulation. It has been shown that the decrease of the beam current amplitude with the length of the drift channel as well as the transformation of the beam energy distribution via its cross section may be explained by incomplete neutralization of the beam space charge at the stage of beam current rising.

articleTitle: 10 kV square wave generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A 10 kV square wave generator was constructed and tested. The generator consists of a DC high voltage source, a pulse forming line (PFL) made from 50 ohm commercial cable, a spark gap switch filled with pressurized nitrogen and a pulse transmission line (PTL) made from the same cable as PFL. By changing the PFL length the pulse width of the generator could be changed. The amplitude of the output voltage pulse varying from 3 kV to 10 kV could be easily obtained by changing the nitrogen pressure. Experiments show that the rise time t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of square wave output from the generator is in the range of 14.1 ns to 1.5 ns when the nitrogen pressure filled in the spark gap varies from 0.2 MPa to 0.7 MPa. It was found that t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> is proportional to p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1.78</sup>,which is different from the result of t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∝</sup>p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5/6</sup>, derived basing on the famous J.C.Martin formula. The 0.4mm gap filled with pressurized nitrogen of 0.7 MPa was broken down at an electric field as high as 500 kV/cm, which made t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> much shorter.

articleTitle: Advances in cherenkov relativistic backward-wave oscillators
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The paper provides a review of experimental research on a backward-wave oscillator with a resonant wave reflector (BWO-RR) which provides frequency tuning within 11 %, extremely high microwave peak power (up to 5 GW in the X-band and 0.2 GW in the K-band), and 35 % efficiency.

articleTitle: A resistive BPM for Mini-LIA
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A prototype of resistive BPM (Beam Position Monitor) was designed and built for Mini-LIA. The design parameters and bench test results are presented. A beam displacement nearly 1mm off-axis can be observed. The relationship between the signal amplitude and decay time constant to current rising time was studied. In conclusion, some factors and phenomenon in the experiment are analyzed

articleTitle: Relationship of pulsed permeability of magnetic cores with annealing Metglas and interlayer insulation films to applied voltage slope
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Magnetic core is a crucial part of Inductive Voltage Adder, which the magnetization properties of the core at the voltage pulse with fast rise time directly influences the co-coupling effect between the primary and secondary. The experimental results indicate that the characteristic parameter V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>/(S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>·t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) has an important impact on pulsed relative permeability of magnetic core (µ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf>) and hysteresis shape, while has little effect on magnetic flux density swing, and at the parameter of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>/(S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>·t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) is equal to about 100V/ns · cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,the parameter of µ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf> of magnetic core sample is equal to about from 200 to 400, when the parameter of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>/(S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>·t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) decreases to 10V/ns · cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the parameter of µ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf> of magnetic core sample increased to about 3000, while the magnetic flux density swing keeps about constant 2.2T.

articleTitle: Status of high power ion beams research at Northwest Institute of Nuclear Technology
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: High power ion beams are potentially useful for inertial confinement fusion and material processing, etc. Fruitful progresses have been achieved in the generation and diagnostics of high power ion beams at Northwest Institute of Nuclear Technology in China. The high power ion beams presently are being produced on Flash II accelerator and 200kV accelerator in pinch diode. The method for enhancing the ratio of ion to electron current is to increase the electron residence time by pinching the electron flow. Furthermore electron beam pinching can be combined with electron reflexing to achieve ion beams with even higher efficiency and intensity. The anode plasma is generated by anode foil bombarded with electron and anode foil surface flashover. High power ion beams have been produced with a current of 160kA and an energy of 500keV corresponding to an ion beam peak power of about 80GW on FLASH II accelerator. The ion number and current of high power ion beams were determined by monitoring delayed radioactivity from nuclear reactions induced in a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>C target by the proton beams. The prompt γ-rays and diode bremsstrahlung X-rays were measured with PIN semi-conductor detector and plastic scintillator detector. The current density distribution of ion beam were measured with biased ion collector array. The ion beams were also recorded with a CR-39 detector. Thermal behavior and dynamic effect of high power ion beams on metallic materials were investigated in the recent years.

articleTitle: Characterization of the rod-pinch diode at 1 MV as a radiography source
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The rod-pinch diode (RPD) is a kind of new X-ray source for flash radiographic applications, especially in the small-scale hydrodynamic experiments. According to theoretical analysis and the generator parameters, the 1 MV rod pinch diode has been designed and studied experimentally. The dose is measured with thermo-luminescent detectors through aluminum hemispherical end-plate (1-cm thick) at 1 m from the rod tip. The size of the radiation source is determined by measuring its edge spread function. The angular distribution of radiation from rod-pinch diode is also examined with angular dose measurements. As results, 1.21 to 1.45 rad at 1 m in the forward direction (0°) are achieved in 18.1 to 27.5 ns FWHM pulses. The spot sizes are 0.9 to 1.1 mm (LANL definition) for 1-mm-diameter blunt tungsten rods and 0.8 mm for 1-mm-diameter tapered tungsten rods. Measured angular distributions indicate that the dose increases monotonically from 0° to 90° by a factor of 1.28 to 1.43 both for blunt and tapered rods and suggest that the radiation still exhibits anisotropy at 1 MV.

articleTitle: Main types of explosive opening switches and their switching parameters
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The results of the research of the switching parameters of three types of explosive current opening switches used for the energy output from the inductive storages to the load in a microsecond time range are presented. The operation of the current opening switches with foil and ribbed barrier, with foil and barrier the ribs of which have metal patches, and the opening switches on dielectric jet-streams has been studied.

articleTitle: 1D and 2D circuit-code modeling of the refurbished Z accelerator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Now that the refurbishment of the Z machine at Sandia is complete we are routinely operating with currents over 26 MA into various loads. With routine operation we are able to measure current and voltage throughout the machine and compare with circuit code predictions. These measurements have motivated improvements to the original model to include two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) sub-circuits. In this paper we describe a full-machine (36 module), one-dimensional (1D) circuit model of Z using the Bertha code developed at the Naval Research Laboratory. We also describe a model that uses 2D sub-modules. In addition, we discuss plans for implementing a 3D circuit model to allow investigating azimuthal effects that can be important for tailoring the rise time, shape, and length of the Z output pulse. Pulse tailoring on Z is achieved by staggering the timing of the various pulsed-forming modules, and by operating individual modules in either long or short-pulse modes. Since the individual lines combine at a large diameter and are separated azimuthally, transit-time effects can be important for determining transient field enhancements at the vacuum insulator and in the vacuum transmission lines, as well as pulse shape. Finally, we compare the 1D and 2D models with data, and provide predictions for both short and long pulse modes for various load configurations.

articleTitle: Progress in Z-pinch at NINT
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Experiments on Z-pinch has been carried out based on a 2 MA pulsed power facility. Gas puff and wire array liners were tested at current 1.4 ∼ 2.1 MA with rise time 80 ∼ 100 ns. For Krypton specific mass of 23 and 47 µg/cm, soft X-ray yield of 55 and 62 kJ, radiation power of 1.9 and 1.7 TW have been obtained, with imploding time of 90 and 118 ns corresponding to current of 1.4 and 1.5 MA and rise time of 80 and 96 ns. For tungsten specific mass of 182 µg/cm, array diameter 12 mm, wire diameter 5 µm, wire number 48 and wire space 0.8 mm, soft X-ray yield of 32 kJ and radiation power of 1.3 TW were obtained with imploding time of 140 ns corresponding to current 1.6 MA and rise time of ∼100 ns. Double nested neon puff liner was tested with keV level X-ray radiation power observed to be greater than that achieved using single liners. 5 filtered XRDs were used to measure X-ray waveform and energy spectrum. A nanosecond, two energy region, 4-framing (for each energy region) soft X-ray imaging camera with 1.8 ns temporal resolution and 1.2 ns timing error was developed to monitor the temporal and spatial evolution of the Z-pinch liner. A nanosecond 4-framing ultraviolet camera was employed to observe the liner's motion during implosion. Total soft X-ray energy was measured by a nickel foil bolometer. Leading (precursor) plasma in the case of tungsten wire array and zip effect in the case of gas puff were observed during implosion. Regarding theoretical approach, driving current waveform will obviously influence initial liner parameter scaling, and maximum imploding kinetic energy per unit liner length can be 0.9 times the square of driving current amplitude multiplying by the natural algorithm of the ratio of initial liner diameter to the final.

articleTitle: Plasma heating in the multimirror trap GOL-3 by prolongated pulse REB
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: To analyze fusion prospects of E-beam heating the plasma in multimirror trap, the beam generator U-2 at the GOL-3 facility was modified for prolongation of 9μs beam pulse. Energy transfer from the beam to plasma column was investigated on the base of measurements of the energy distribution functions both plasma electrons (Thomson scattering of Nd-glass laser light) and beam electrons (multifoil analyzer). This measuring with diamagnetic signals gave new knowledge on dynamics of plasma heating by relativistic E-beam.

articleTitle: Plasma dynamics in different kinds of experiments at megaampere range on S-300 machine
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This article presents experiments on a high-current magnetically insulated transmission line (MITL) and a mega-ampere X-pinch. It was shown that the time during which a MITL preserves its transmission properties at high linear current densities (5-7 MA/cm) corresponds to the requirements of the conceptual fusion reactor. The traditional X-pinch dynamics existence at electrical currents 1.3-2.3 MA has also been demonstrated together with the applicability of the main dynamic features (linear mass-current scaling, in particular) for considerably lower currents. It has been shown that the forming plasma object has the radiation luminosity higher than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> W/(cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>sr) in a photon energy range of 1-3 keV, the size of the hot spot ~20 μm, and the radiation power ~120 GW; these parameters are several times higher than the values obtained previously. The energy emitted by the molybdenum X-pinch in the range of 2.5-3 keV was shown to be no less than 15 J.

articleTitle: Simulation research of a novel MILO
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A new magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) with two extracted vanes and coaxial varied impedance load structure was presented and analyzed. Simulation showed them to substantially outperform previous MILO variants, predicting efficiencies up to about 20%. Two distinct mechanisms were shown to contribute to this high efficiency. The first was the two extracted vanes adopted which usage was like the extracted vanes of the relativistic klystron. The second was the coaxial varied impedance (CVI) load structure adopted which changed the load impedance equals the MILO impedance and also could separate the operated beam to leave the operating region. Under the diode voltage of 550kV, the current of 28kA, microwave with the output power of 3GW and the frequency of 2.76GHz had been got in the simulation.

articleTitle: Signal compensation of transmission cable of QiangGuang I accelerator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The coaxial cable length of metrical system of QiangGuang I accelerator is about 50 meters. The pulse signals consequentially come into being the phenomena of distortion and aberration. With the development and need of experiments, the signals conform with the source signals are needed. Generally, there are two methods that can compensate the distortion signals. The one is making use of the compensating net called the hardware compensation. Another is making use of simulation by software called the software compensation. The paper introduce the application of two ways based on QG I accelerator.

articleTitle: Calibration of the energy response for the soft X-ray spectrometer with the BSRF
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Special important station and application of BSRF in the Z-pinch physics study are introduced first. Beijing Synchrotron Radiation Facility (BSRF) used special operation mode with the storage ring electron energy 2.5GeV, beam current 130~250mA, photon energy region 50~1800eV. We inserted metal filters in the 3W1B for absorbing higher harmonics. In this paper, the methods of calibrating the soft X-ray spectrometer elements are reported and the calibration curves are given. At last, We analyzed the difference of the experimental data and the theoretical calculation.

articleTitle: Electron beams under fore pump pressure range: Generation and some applications
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The paper presents review of recent results of development and some applications of plasma cathode sources generating electron beams in so called fore-pump pressure range (1÷15 Pa). This kind of electron sources has no alternatives for electron beam production under relatively high pressure. Essential progress was reached recently in generation of continues electron beams with energy up to 20 keV for narrow focusing and 10 keV for ribbon configurations. Several specific problems were solved for e-beam generation at this pressure range. Main of them are: high probability for electrical breakdown of accelerating gap, essential influence of back ion stream both on emission electrode and emitting plasma, formation of secondary plasma in beam propagation area as well as intensive beam-plasma interaction. Specific peculiarities take place in case of ribbon type electron beam generation. They are local maximums in current density distribution across the beam. Due to rather high pressure, electron beams may be used as for metal melting, evaporation, treatment, so for dielectric processing: melting, welding, drilling etc.

articleTitle: Design and test of small helical generator with load current up to MA
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The design and principal experiments of a multi branches helical EMG with a 25nH inductive load have been carried out in this paper. According to the results of the code MFCG8-7 based on the circuit model, an EMG-125 type generator has been designed and tested. The EMG-125 generator is of 900mm in length, 125mm in diameter, and the charging explosive weight 2.7kg. A series of experiments show that, there would be serious breakdowns inside the generator if the input current were out of the limit of 8kA (the limit of the input energy is about 2 kJ). In the case of input current 8kA, the peak current 3MA has been measured on the inductive load that is 0.3MA less than the calculated result without magnetic flux losses. The maximal energy on the inductive load is 100kJ with the peak gain of 50. The calculated results agree with the experimental results when the calibrated coefficient of magnetic flux losses is set as 0.03.

articleTitle: Design of a high-power linear induction prototype cell at megahertz repetition rate burst mode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A linear induction prototype cells expected to work at a train of three 240 kV pulses separated by 500 ns, has been designed. The cell is composed of magnetic cores immersed in oil, a gap with curved stainless steel electrodes, a solenoid magnet, and a nylon insulator. This paper describes the various issues considered in the design of the prototype cell with emphasis on high-voltage characterization. The high-voltage performance of the cell is also reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Self breakdown properties and optimum of insulator envelope for MV gas switches
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Two insulator bracing type MV gas switches are developed. One switch's HV electrode is cantilever and the insulator envelope is integrated. The other's HV electrode is out of insulator envelope and the brace cylinder is sectioned. Through self breakdown experiments and electrostatic field simulations, the optimum design of insulator envelopes is discussed and the reason for puncturing on the envelope of cantilever switch is given. The self breakdown properties of switches are discussed as well.

articleTitle: An energy spectrometer for detecting flash X-ray spectra from 200 to 3000keV
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The basic theory and experimental results obtained in measuring energy spectra of time- resolved high energy pulsed X-ray are reported. MCNP code was employed to calculate the energy deposition of high energy photons on the energy spectrometer. The waveforms of high energy pulsed X-ray created on the “Qiangguang-I” accelerator were measured by using the energy spectrometer. According to the deposited energy and integral data, the time-resolved high pulsed x-ray energy spectrum was obtained. By using the voltage and current waveforms of the diode, the energy spectrum was calculated in details. The results were agreed with that measured with the experimental energy spectrum.

articleTitle: Applications of series resonant power supply in Tesla transformer
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A circuit topology which can prevent the series resonant power supply in a Tesla transformer from damage induced by the reversal voltage on the storage capacitor is presented. The circuit is based on current-limiting resistor and auxiliary capacitor which can restrict the over current in the rectifier of series resonant power supply. Moreover, adoption of the auxiliary capacitor can raise the average power output of the power supply due to the increase of initial voltage on the storage capacitor. When reversal voltage on the storage capacitor is zero and the auxiliary capacitor is one quarter of the storage capacitor, analysis shows the average power output can be raised 33%. Computation of charging accuracy and optimization of current-limiting resistance are also discussed.

articleTitle: High power microwave short pulse generation at S-band using multi-resonant cavity
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Experiment of obtaining HPM pulse using Multi resonant cavities pulse compress setup is presented. The pulse compression system works at S band and the resonance frequency is 2.85 GHz. With a 10MW and 2.0 μs input pulse, the system can generate two pulses each with more then 100 MW pulse power and 10ns pulse duration, the energy efficiency has a range of 10%~30%, and the average energy efficiency is about 20%.

articleTitle: Characterization of intense pulsed aluminum ion beam by magnetically insulated diode with vacuum arc ion source
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Intense pulsed heavy ion beam is expected to be applied to materials processing including surface modification and ion implantation. For those applications, it is very important to generate high-purity ion beams with various ion species. A magnetically insulated ion diode with an active ion source of a vacuum arc plasma gun has been developed in order to generate pulsed metallic ion beams. When the ion diode was operated at diode voltage ≈200 kV, diode current ≈15 kA and pulse duration ≈100 ns, the ion beam with an ion current density of >; 200 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was obtained at 50 mm downstream from the anode. From Thomson parabola spectrometer measurement, the ion beam consists of aluminum ions (Al<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, Al<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and Al<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>) of energy 60-300 keV and the proton impurities of energy 60-150 keV. The purity of the beam was estimated to be 89%.

articleTitle: Investigation of 4 MV coaxial-triplate water self-breaking switch
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A high power pulse device, primary test stand (PTS), is under-developed at the Institute of Fluid Physics, CAEP. In order to study the key techniques, the prototype module was built firstly. The prototype module contains Marx generator, intermediate store capacitor, laser triggered gas switch, water pulse forming line, water self-breaking switch, water transmission line and water resistance load. A 4 MV coaxial-triplate multi-channel water dielectric self-breaking switch is designed for water pulse forming line section of the prototype module. The water self-breaking switch contains supporting hardware and three linear arrayed self-breaking gaps. Each gap of the switch is plane to pin electrode configuration. The designable and experimental methods of the water self-breaking switch operating at about 100 ns pulse duration (FWHM) are investigated thoroughly. The jitter, breaking voltage, sum of the channels, electric field analyze, and electric diagnosis are investigative objects of this paper. The working voltage is 3.5 MV and current is 500 kA. The jitter and the inductance of the switch are 3.0 ns and about 40 nH respectively.

articleTitle: Calculations on dispersion relation and coupling impedance of plasma coupled-cavity SWS
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The electromagnetic field accurate expressions in the external axial magnetic field are obtained from the Maxwell's equations. Further, the flux of energy inside the plasma filled drift channel is presented. Some of the property of cavity passband dispersion and coupling impedance of plasma-filled coupled-cavities slow wave structure in different plasma density and magnetic field conditions is analyzed according to the numerical calculation.

articleTitle: Nanosecond high-voltage generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Design of compact high voltage generator is described. The generator consists from: capacitive energy storage (2kJ); vacuum switch (200 kA); switch controlling device (40kV); Tesla transformer (20/1); glycerin pulse forming line (2.7 Ohm): oil switch (400-750 kV) with control unit; high-voltage insulator; self-magnetically insulated vacuum line; load. The generator produces high-voltage pulses with amplitude in the range of 350-500 kV and pulse duration 10-20 ns. It is meant for powering microwave sources, vacuum diodes or X-ray sources. Calculations of the electric field strength distribution in the generator units, reliability of their operation and results of test are presented.

articleTitle: A repetitive high voltage pulse adder based on solid state switches
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A repetitive high voltage pulse modulator based on solid state switches with insolated recharge is described. All capacitors in the modulator are recharged by a corresponding transformer separately through magnetic core transformers by a common high frequency power supply. This configuration simplifies the isolation design and arrangement. This scheme is suitable for work at high repetitive rate discharge due to its high charge efficiency. At the same time it retains the inherent switch protection capability of a solid-state Marx modulator. In our present work, a 22-stage test modulator has been built and has been successfully operated at repetitive rate of 20kHz, output voltage of 20kV, rise time of 150ns and pulse width of 3μs. The primary experiments verified the system feasibility. A system with higher parameters is under way.

articleTitle: The design of the double shell gas puff for Qiangguang I generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The double shell gas puff is applied extensively in Z pinch experiments because it can reduce R-T instability during the implosion phase. In this paper the design of the double shell gas puff is introduced, including the whole configuration, the synchronization of the gas release valves and the airproof of the inner and the outer chambers. The main factors which affect the airproof of the chambers are analyzed and the parameters of the springs are been calculated. The gas release system consisting of the winding, iron core and the pull rod is also simulated; the result proved that the system can completely satisfied the demand of the Z pinch experiments. A last the result of the testing experiment on Qiangguang I is given and it proves the practicality of the double shell gas puff.

articleTitle: Frequency characteristics of TE11 mode enhanced coaxial vircator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Due to poloidal-asymmetry electron emitting, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode output of high-power microwave (HPM) is unavoidable in coaxial vircator. In order to obtain a pure mode output, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode enhanced design by opposed section electron emitting is applied with more advantages. As two-dimensional effect along poloidal direction is coursed, the frequency of microwave generated is shifted in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode enhanced coaxial vircator compared with the thoroughly coaxial one. Frequency characteristics of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode enhanced coaxial vircator are studied numerically by the 3-D particle-in-cell (PIC) code UNIPIC and experimentally on a high-power pulse modulator. Simulations results show that a stable TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode output is generated nearly with a point frequency in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode enhanced geometry, which is a little lower than that in the thoroughly coaxial geometry. In experiments, nearly point frequency and stable TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode output is also obtained and the effect of diode voltage, anode-cathode gap and electron beams width are investigated. The results show that with higher diode voltage, smaller anode-cathode gap and larger electron beams width, the frequency of microwave generated is higher, especially electron beams width has the same degree effect with diode voltage and anode-cathode gap, which is well agreed with simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of a TM01-TE01 transmission line for high-power microwave applications
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In this paper, we report the design methods and numerical results for a kind of high-power microwave (HPM) circular waveguide transmission line, which has a 90-degree bend to change the wave propagating direction for certain purposes, and meanwhile, also acts as a TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> converter, transforming the HPM sources generating TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode into the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode. A type of mode conversion sequences, i.e. TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>, is proposed. In the sequences, a 90-degree-bend circular waveguide TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode converter is adopted to change the wave propagating direction. Besides, compact, linear TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode converters are designed to perform the mode conversion from TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode to TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode. The transmission efficiency of the designed transmission line is 97.9% at 3.5 GHz, and the bandwidth for efficiency>;90% is 5.3%.

articleTitle: Time-resolved measurement system using Optical Transition Radiation for electron beam of high energy and high current
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The technology using Optical Transition Radiation (OTR)which is a main method for measuring the electron beam of high energy and high current has been developed for the past ten years. OTR characterized by the ultra-fast response, high resolution and capability of measuring both spatial and angular profiles of an electron beam. It also can measure the beam energy and divergence. A time-resolved measurement results of an electron beam produced by Linear Induction Accelerator ( LIA ) can provide much more detail information so that many problems about the beam transmission can be known well. Such a time-resolved measurement system has been developed recently in our lab and put into operation. It provides an on-line beam diagnostic method for a 18.5MeV, 2kA, 90ns(FWHM) electron pulse by Dragon I[1]. The beam emittance and its variation during the 90ns pulse are obtained in 10ns time interval. The time-resolved results of about 2200π.mm.mrad have been obtained from Dragon I.

articleTitle: Study of Ar K-shell spectra from Z-pinch experiments on Yang Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Ar K-shell Spectra were measured using an elliptical crystal spectrometer in gas-puff Z-pinch experiments performed on Yang Accelerator (peak current 800 kA, rise time 90 ns). To estimate from the spectra the electron temperature of the plasma, a collisional-radiative (CR) model was developed. By comparing the line ratio of Lyα and Hea derived from the experimental results with those predicted by the model, time and space averaged electron temperature value was obtained.

articleTitle: Optimization of high-voltage nanosecond pulse compression
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The work is directed on an increase in an energy effectiveness of the existing compact devices, intended for the energy compression of the nanosecond time range pulses [1]. Devices consist of high impedance (HL) and forming (FL) lines and high-pressure spark gas discharger. In contrast to the device [1] with a serial discharge circuit of FL, the version of circuit with a parallel discharge for the load of lines HL and FL is proposed. The calculations, which show the energy effectiveness of this scheme, are given. Converter with the parallel discharge circuit on base [1] is developed. The converter with parallel discharge circuit increased peak pulse power additionally on 17% in comparison with serial discharge converter for a case of initial pulse with rise time ~0.5 ns. The voltage amplitude of the initial nanosecond pulse 4 ns was increased from 145 kV to 195 kV (across the load 45 Ohm) with the time compression of pulse to ~0.8 ns. A real increase of the peak power across the load 45 Ohm reached 1.8 when calculated value 2.5. Device, which form two fixed pulse waveforms 210 kV, 0.8 ns and 250 kV, 0.45 ns by converting nanosecond pulse with an amplitude 160 kV and peaked rise time to 0. 3 ns is made.

articleTitle: High-current electron accelerator based on pulse generator with vacuum insulation
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This report presents the description of the electron accelerator on basis of the powerful small-inductive pulse generator with vacuum insulation. Using of the generator with vacuum insulation allows to simplify considerably a design of the accelerator having excluded from it an intermediate store. The accelerator tests results and also the experimental results on obtaining of the large cross-section ribbon beams with the ~500-700 keV electron energy are reported. Distinctive feature of the accelerator configuration for the ribbon beam generation is the cathode arrangement in parallel to the generator column axis. It is shown that in such configuration it is possible to receive practically homogeneous ribbon beam with the current density of 25 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the cross-section of 25×100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Sectionalized explosive current opening switch
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The paper considers the design of the sectionalized explosive current opening switch which allows increasing the power of the current pulse in the load. The results of testing of the sectionalized opening switch operation on plane models are presented. The results of the experiment with the pulsed source of current on the basis of HEMG and 10-section cylindrical current opening switch are described.

articleTitle: Applications of treatment design in the study on the characteristic of a detector
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This paper described two experimental designs. Based on the data of experiments, the characteristic of a detector was found efficiently. A regression model was developed through designs and analysis of multi-factor orthogonal experiments and orthogonal, rotatable regression experiments. The regression model gave very close results to the experiment samples.

articleTitle: 20-MW desktop free-electron laser at THz frequencies
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: We numerically study the generation of periodically bunched electrons from a 6 MeV photocathode electron gun driven by a beat-wave laser with a beat frequency at THz frequencies. We then inject the electrons into a single-pass FEL undulator. Due to the prebunched electrons, the quick build-up of the FEL power can overcome the space-charge debunching force. With nominal beam parameters and an initial bunching factor of 0.2, the FEL can reach nearly 20-MW saturation power at 4 THz in a ∼0.5 m distance in the wiggler. The length of this 20MW THz FEL, from the beginning of the electron gun to the end of the undulator, is less than a meter.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical studies on relativistic magnetron with axial extraction
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: • Modified configuration of MDO • Particle-in-cell simulation by “MAGIC” → 1050 MW, 2.55 GHz, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf>, 31% • Experiments on “ETIGO-IV” • General agreement between experimental and numerical results

articleTitle: The blur of system for FTO proton radiography
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The blur of system for the FTO proton radiography (PRAD), which represents the quality of radiographic image, was studied. It is shown that the characteristics of the blurs in PRAD are obviously different from x-ray radiography. In PRAD, the size of the source is no longer the dominant factor as x-ray radiography. But container, Even for 50 GeV PRAD, the blur of the steel container with 5 cm thickness and 200 cm radius is larger than 2.3 mm. While others are less than 1.0 mm. The container blur is proportional to the multiple Coulomb scatter (MCS) angle and the radius of the container. All the mismatched angle blurs are proportional to chromatic aberration coefficient, the mismatched angle and the relative momentum loss. And the object blur is proportional to its thickness and MCS angle.

articleTitle: Microsecond plasma opening switches operation scenario
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The regularities of current closing and tearing in the microsecond megaampere plasma opening switches are considered. It is outlined the switch conduction current scaling which is determined by the plasma acceleration by the magnetic piston, and its comparison with the experimental results. It is considered the current channel structure formation which is determined by diffusion and convective magnetic field transport into the accelerated plasma flow. On basis of the experimental results, it is given the switch voltage scaling depending on the switch parameters. It is discussed problem of the switch reverse closing restricting the energy output efficiency from an inductive storage to a load.

articleTitle: High power and repetitively pulsed operation of a Relativistic Extended-Interaction-Cavity Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: An Oscillator of Relativistic Extended Interaction Cavity (REICO) is presented and manufactured successfully for the first time. The problems encountered with in the initial experiment are investigated, and the pillboxes and the triaxial output cavity of the REICO are optimized in this paper. The mode-competition of modulation was overcome by adjusting the gap width of pillboxes. The output microwave pulse width increasing from 20ns to 38ns and the repetition rates increasing from 15Hz to 100Hz are improved after optimizing the structures of the electron beams collection and the triaxial cavity. Using a 900kV, 16kA, 45ns electron beam, 4.1GW radiated power was extracted in 38ns FWHM pulses at 2.86GHz and 100pps. The power efficiency is 26%, and the energy efficiency is 22%. The average power is 16 kW.

articleTitle: High quality pseudospark electron beams for millimetre-wave sources
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Experimental studies of the production and propagation of an electron beam from a multi-gap pseudospark discharge chamber are presented. A beam up to 680 A was measured at the anode when a three-gap pseudospark underwent a breakdown at an applied DC voltage of 23 kV. This beam can propagate further downstream as far as 20 cm in length in a gaseous environment (pressure = 60 mtorr) with no guiding magnetic field. The recorded beam traces at two different positions along the drift tube and the cross-section image of the electron beam further confirm that the transport of the electron beam was based on the neutralization of the space-charge of the electron beam due to the ionization of the gas molecules by the beam itself. The beam produced is of very small size of 1-3 mm in diameter and is ideal to drive high frequency radiation due to its small beam size and the compactness of the device. Therefore higher energy electron beam pulses were further generated from a 14-gap pseudospark discharges powered by a pulsed power system (a cable pulser) capable of producing 120 ns duration and 170 kV voltage pulses. The beam produced is of very small size of 1-3 mm in diameter and is measured with current up to 110 A. Interactions between the electron beam and a Ka-band and W-band slow wave structure were simulated and designed. The beam-wave interaction experiments were conducted and microwave pulses were detected successfully from the 14-gap pseudospark-based electron beam-wave interaction experiments.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the voltage distribution of tesla transformer's taper windings
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: By use the taper high voltage windings, the Tesla transformer with compact structure can be built. However, the flashover between coils will occur because of un-uniform of the voltage distribution along the windings. Therefore, researching the voltage distribution of the Tesla transformer, improving the distribution by appropriate method and designing optimized structure of the windings would highly improve repetitive ability of the transformer, which have theoretical and engineering significance for the Tesla transformer's working in reliable and security. In order to study the voltage distribution on the pulse transformer's taper windings, according to the structure of the factual pulse transformer's taper windings, the voltage of a uniform tesla transformer's windings was measured in the paper. It is shown that the voltage distribution of taper winding is not uniform, and the distributed curve of it's interturn voltage is U shape with 100ns pulse. Based on the results, the methods to improve the distribution of the tape winding were bring forwards by measuring and analyzing the voltage distribution of other taper windings with different structure. These results can give some references to interturn insulation designs of Tesla transformer's windings.

articleTitle: The simulation of electron beam formation in initial stage of gas discharge
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: There was elaborated the discharge development model based on particle-in-cell method taking into the account volume charge and collisions by method Monte-Carlo. The simulation of the initial stage of gas discharge on conditions that E/P>;1kV/cm/Torr showed that in the interval of ~10 ps electron beam of run-away electrons was formed nearby cathode. This beam consists of electrons emitted from cathode and electrons arising as a result of gas ionization. It was showed that duration of the beam of run-away electrons nearby cathode mainly depend on outer electrical field screening by plasma and was equal to 10-20 ps.

articleTitle: High-voltage pulse generators for microwave radiation sources
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A set of high-voltage pulse generators is described. They are used for generation of gigawatt microwave radiation pulses in vircator or relativistic BWO with ~50 Ohm diode impedance. The first two generators are based on inductive energy storage and an exploding wires switch. The output voltage and the power of the first generator are ~600 kV and 10 GW, respectively. The second generator provides the 20 GW and 60 GW pulses in the 50 Ohm and 12 Ohm vacuum diodes with FWHM ~300 ns. The third generator based on Marx's generator and water forming line provides the 1 MV pulse on the 50 Ohm diode. The generators design and the testing results are presented.

articleTitle: High power microwave research at the university of strathclyde
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation. This paper presents electron beam generations; electron guns; cathodes; coherent microwave generations; gyrotrons; gyro-TWA, and; gyro-BWO; Cherenkov BWO and; dielectric Cherenkov.

articleTitle: Phenomenon of electrical tree in repetitive nanosecond high electrical field pulse
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The phenomenon of electrical tree growing under repetitive nanosecond high voltage pulses (fwhm 70ns) is researched in the paper. The single-magnetic pulse compression system is used in these experiments. The pure polyethylene material is adopted as the experimental sample. To reduce the random dispersion of experiments' results, every test sample had six needle electrodes with a uniform spacing distribution. The experiments' results show the correlation between tree growth rate and the related factors such as voltage and frequency. The interested phenomenon of stress fracture inside the samples is found in the experiments.

articleTitle: Pulse shortening in the improved magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator (MILO) is a crossed field device designed specifically to generate microwave power at the gigawatt level, which is a major hotspot in the field of high-power microwaves (HPM) research at present. An improved MILO has been developed in our laboratory. When the improved MILO is driven by a 550kV, 54kA, 80ns electron beam, HPM is generated with power of 3.2 GW, frequency of about 1.76 GHz, and duration of 40 ns. In order to lengthen the duration of the radiated microwave pulse, a long-pulse accelerator, whose voltage is about 450 kV and impedance is about 15 Ω, is employed to drive the improved MILO. In experiments, the diode voltage is increased gradually from about 350 kV to about 460 kV. When the diode voltages are 375 kV, 438 kV and 458 kV, the corresponding microwave power are 0.7 GW, 1.8 GW and 2.3 GW, and the pulse duration are 110 ns, 100 ns, and 65 ns respectively. It is obvious that pulse shortening is observed in the experiments. The simulation and experimental results confirm that the leading reason for pulse shortening is the remarkable voltage variation in the experiments. In conclusion, a sufficiently flat voltage pulse is crucial to achieving a longer microwave pulse.

articleTitle: High spectral resolved spectroscopic diagnostics for wire array z-pinch plasmas
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Spectrograph with spherically bent mica crystals have provided time-integrated spectra and monochromatic self-emission images of aluminum wire array z-pinch implosions on the Qiangguang-I pulsed power generator. Although 1–3 millimeter diameter of plasma column greatly broadened the line width on the detector, spectral resolution of about 1000–3000 could be realized with this focusing spectrograph, which was much better than that of spectrographs with flat or convex curved crystals. The detector was arranged so that the spectra were axially resolved. Self-emission images of wire array z-pinch plasmas showed presence of bright spots in the plasma column.

articleTitle: W-band Gyro-BWO using a helically corrugated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Presented in this paper is the design of a W-Band Gyro-BWO with a helically corrugated waveguide and a cusp electron gun. The interaction region has been constructed with good accuracy and microwave results measured using a vector network analyzer are given. The microwave dispersion agrees well with analytical and numerical theory. The transmission loss of this helically corrugated waveguide was measured to be ∼1dB over the frequency range (84 – 104GHz). A cusp electron gun has been designed to generate a 1.5A, 40kV electron beam with an adjustable pitch angle (α) of up to 3. The beam was optimized through numerical simulation with an axial velocity spread, ΔV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>/V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>, of 7% and Δα/α, of 10.4% at α=1.65. From simulation of the beam-wave interaction the maximum output power from the Gyro-BWO was predicted to be 10kW (CW) at 17% efficiency, with a 3dB frequency tuning range of ∼84–104GHz.

articleTitle: Pulse power device and beam driven target as tools for high energy density science
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Dense plasmas driven by pulse power devices and/or intense ion beams were evaluated, concerning researches on high-energy density and warm dense matter physics. A warm and dense plasma was produced using pulse power driven exploding discharges in water. A high temperature plasma was formed in a pulse power device by electro-magneticaly driven strong shock wave. A quasi-statically tamped target has been proposed to make a well-defined, warm dense state for equation of state studies based on ion beam heated target.

articleTitle: Generation narrow focusing beams in plasma cathode electron guns
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The work purpose is producing of the focused electron beam with minimal diameter and divergence in a plasma cathode gun. Researches of influence of an emitting plasma surface position in electron-optical system of a gun on electron beam parameters are executed. The measurement technique of current density distribution is developed. For the first time in system with the plasma emitter beams with energy 30–60 keV, power about some kilowatt, with diameter of the order 250 microns and a divergence no more than 0,05 degrees are received.

articleTitle: A high power 390 GHz harmonic gyrotron based on cusp electron gun
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The design and simulation of a harmonic gyrotron based on a cusp electron gun is presented. The gyrotron is operated at the 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> electron cyclotron harmonic with an output frequency of ~390 GHz and mode pattern of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">71</sub>. A large orbit electron beam with energy of 40 keV, beam current of 1.5A and an adjustable pitch alpha from 1 to 3 from a cusp gun is used to drive the beam-wave interaction. Smooth cylindrical waveguide and slotted structures have been studied as interaction cavities. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulation results of these structures will be presented.

articleTitle: High power particle beams researches in IFP
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: “Presents a collection of slides covering the following topics: high power particle beams; linear induction accelerators; and Z-pinch accelerators.

articleTitle: Conceptual design of a 2.5 MV linear transformer driver generator for X-ray radiography
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: LTD (Linear Transformer Driver) is a new technology developed recent years suitable of building compact high voltage short-pulse generator. RPD (Rod pinch diode) can provide very small diameter (even sub-millimeter) X-ray source for pulsed radiography. Combination of LTD and RPD would allow building compact FXR (Flash X-ray Radiography) generator with excellent performance. A conceptual design of a FXR generator was made based on LTD and RPD technology. New approach to modulate the pulse shape was introduced. The output voltage, impedance and FWHM are 2.5 MV, 45 Ω and 60 ns respectively.

articleTitle: Simulation study of a novel all solid, long pulse, high power pulse modulator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In this paper is designed a novel all solid pulsed power system of high repetition rates, long pulse, high reliability, long life, and compact. This system is composed of BOOST circuit, LC circuit, pulsed transformer, magnetic compression circuit, and strip line. The theoretical analysis and simulation of the BOOST circuit and magnetic compression circuit are given. The optimization of the system is done by Pspice software. An output pulse of 55kV voltage, 132kA current and 400ns pulse-width is obtained.

articleTitle: 500kV compact repetitive Marx generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A 500kV compact repetitive Marx generator with double-charging way was developed and tested. This generator is composed of 12 inductively isolated capacitor stages parallel charged through the rod-shaped inductors with the magnetic core. The charging time was shortened in the pulse charging mode. The field distortion gas switches which realized serial discharge and the non-inductive capacitors were arranged in a cross-strip row, and together with trigger sharpen circuit and charging partial circuit were placed in square transformer oil tank, thus, the cramped construction was established. By the analysis and test, output pulse peak voltage is 500kV, the rise time is less than 80ns, the stored-energy in bank of capacitors is about 130J. With a repetition rate of 1Hz∼5Hz, the generator can operate steadily under a pressure of 1.5atm dry-pure SF6.

articleTitle: An advances in relativistic BWOs at repetitive rate
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Advances of repetitively operated relativistic backward wave oscillator (BWOs) is presented. Improvement of operating stability of BWO was obtained based on our earlier BWO operating at 100 Hz repetitive rates through changing the cathode and beam collector. An oil-immersed graphite cathode and water-cooled beam collector were introduced to increase output stability. Experimental results indicate that BWO's efficiency is up to the highest 33 % at optimum diode voltage, which is consistent with numerical simulations. The BWO could stably operate at rates of 100 Hz with microwave output power of over 1 GW, and the continuous time was up to 5 seconds.

articleTitle: Investigation of anode foil stability at high-current electron accelerator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Results of experimental studies of anode foil destruction mechanisms are presented. The experiments have been done on the accelerator with the following parameters: voltage - up to 500 kV, e-beam current - up to 10 kA, pulse duration (FWHM) - 60 ns, pulse repetition rate - up to 3 Hz. It was found out that the formation of cathode spots on the anode foil surface as well as the current in the diode during the positive post-pulses following the main negative pulse of the accelerating voltage are the main reasons for the foil life time limitation. The improvement of the diode impedance matching with the output impedance of the pulsed power generator decreases the energy of the post-pulses and leads to a longer life time of the anode foil. The introduction of an additional anode electrode forming with the cathode a vacuum crowbar switch practically excludes damages of the anode foil and increases its life time up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> pulses.

articleTitle: Review of pulsed power development and applications in Russia
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation. This paper presents pulsed power generators; charges particle beams; Z-pinches and radiation sources; and pulsed power technological applications.

articleTitle: Recent progress on relativistic magnetrons using a transparent cathode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Researchers at the University of New Mexico (UNM) recently proposed that a transparent cathode can significantly improve the output characteristics of magnetrons [1]. Since then, a comprehensive study using particle-in-cell simulations [2] has identified the many benefits of using this cathode. At present we are in the midst of preparations for performing the first experiments at UNM to demonstrate the key features of using a transparent cathode instead of a traditional solid cathode.
