This paper will review the various benefits of operating relativistic and nonrelativistic magnetrons using a transparent cathode. In addition, plans for the initial experiments at the University of New Mexico on an A6 magnetron [3] driven by a short-pulse Sinus-6 accelerator will be presented. Future experiments on an A6 magnetron using a longer pulse (50 ns) accelerator at UNM will also be described, including details on the pulsed power redesign of the UNM PI-110A accelerator.

articleTitle: Experimental research on a 10-stage wave erection Marx generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A 10-stage wave erection Marx generator is designed and set up using 50-kV non-inductive capacitors and solid resistors. The impedance characteristic of the generator is experimentally studied by utilizing a water resistor load with different resistances. For a charging voltage of 40 kV, an output high voltage pulse with amplitude of about 200 kV, full width half maximum (FWHM) of 40~50 ns, and rise time of several ns is obtained on a matched load. This high voltage pulse generator is applied to drive a field-emission diode successfully. For a cathode-anode gap of 15 mm with charging a voltage of 30 kV, the output voltage on the diode is about 154 kV, and the electron beam current is 1.6 kA.

articleTitle: Linear analysis of corrugated-wall waveguides driven by annular beam with finite-strength guiding magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Corrugated-wall waveguides have been widely used in Backward-Wave Oscillators (BWOs) which are commonly drove by annular beam with certain thickness. With finite-strength guiding magnetic field the beam region tends to be dispersive medium and the dielectric tensor makes the axial RF electric field correlative with RF magnetic field even under axisymmetric mode. The linear dispersion relation is obtained according to the described condition by expressing the fields in the beam region as coupled ordinary and extra-ordinary modes. Numerical analysis is carried out using the parameters of a BWO which has been studied in UESTC [1], from which series of the complex angular frequencies assuming real wave number are obtained by varying the magnetic field. Comparison is made with the reported result [2]. The results also show the cyclotron absorption during certain range of the magnetic field.

articleTitle: Effect of emission increasing at the generation of low-energy submillisecond electron beam in the diode with the plasma cathode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The results of investigation of the effect of electron emission increasing in the diode based on a plasma cathode with a grid boundary stabilization of plasma are presented. As a result of investigations it was revealed, that with an increase of pressure while electron beam pulse (100 μs) passing with energy of 15-20 keV in the plasma formed as a result of gas ionization by an electron beam, the emission current increases at a constant discharge current of a plasma cathode and the emission current magnitude can exceed the discharge current in an absolute value. It has been shown that the significant increasing of an electron beam current is provided due to the secondary ion-electron emission originating from the bombardment of an emission electrode surface by ions accelerated from the boundary of anodic plasma.

articleTitle: Primary experimental study on synchronous discharge of ten multi gap multi channel gas switches
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the structures of the ±100kV multi gap multi channel gas switch. The self breakdown performance of ten switches is introduced. A test bed for synchronous discharge is established. Ten switches are arranged in parallel, and then the synchronous discharge is carried out. The cases with different switching coefficients are analyzed. Two types of trigger isolating water resistors are used in the test. The experimental result indicates that 110kA output current with 100ns rise time can be achieved when the switches are filled with 0.16MPa nitrogen, and charged to ±65kV.

articleTitle: A high ratio air-core pulse transformer
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Ultrawideband(UWB) System based on air-core pulse transformer can easily get high repetition frequency and high peak power. Theoretical research was carried on air-core pulse transformer which composed of taper winding. The relationship between transformer's output voltage and coupling coefficient was analyzed. The adaptive values of coupling coefficient was calculated to realize wonderful electric performance. An air-core and high ratio pulse transformer was developed, which can be charged by commercial power. The experiment indicate the output voltage of transformer arrive at 110kV with coupling coefficient being 0.72, When input voltage is 290V.

articleTitle: The “Baikal” project and investigations of radiating Z-pinches at the “Angara-5-1” facility
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In the work presented are the results of the investigations into the physics of implosion of multiple wire arrays from various elements carried out on the Angara-5-1 facility. To study the process of prolonged plasma production for such arrays some microprobes placed inside the liner were applied. As a result a dependence of the time taken by a magnetic field to penetrate the half radius of the liner on its wire substance type has been found. Study into the process of compression both along the pinch radius and axis was carried out in experiments with conic arrays. Such experiments along with calculations permit clarifying 3-D effects arising in compressing these wire arrays. We describe the results produced by a MEVL code for simulation magnetically insolated vacuum transmission lines (MIVL), which are connected in parallel. This simulation has been tested on the Angara-5-I installation. The results of experiments performed on MOL installation for Baikal project about energy transfer at millisecond time scale are presented.

articleTitle: Study of primary power supply of repetitive intense current pulsed accelerator based on super-capacitor
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: According to the characteristic of super-capacitor, the primary power supply of repetitive intense current pulsed accelerator based on super-capacitor is investigated in this paper. The inner resistance of super-capacitor is the key point in its pulse power application, considering the influence of the inner resistance of super-capacitor, the energy loss in the inner resistance of one charging cycle is analyzed, and the number of pulses and the usable voltage scope of super-capacitor are obtained. The simulation of the actual parameters of circuits is carried out, and some results are compared between the simulation and the analysis. At last, some useful conclusions are summarized.

articleTitle: Design considerations for an overmoded MW-class terahertz surface-wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Results of theoretical and numerical simulation studies of a large cross section (overmoded), surface wave oscillator (SWO) with a cylindrical slow wave structure (SWS) are presented. The dispersion relation of the overmoded SWS, which express the phenomenon of mode competition, is calculated, and the distribution of electrical fields in the device is also determined. A novel particle in cell simulation tool is developed, aiming at the design of vacuum electron tubes in the terahertz regime. It is found that the steady-state, single-mode operation in this overmoded situation could be realized by the performance of surface wave at “π” point. Under the condition of 550kV beam voltage and 1kA beam current, 2.5D PIC simulation predicted that the proposed SWO could deliver an output power above 40 MW at the frequency of about 0.144THz with perfect time plot and fine spectrum characteristic.

articleTitle: Experimental study on high pressure hydrogen gas switch breakdown
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The gas switches can be used to produce high power electromagnetic pulses with very fast risetime in the pulsed power systems such as UWB radiate systems, particles accelerators, laser drivers and so on. The hydrogen gas switches have promised in repetitive rate application for its fastest recovery feature. Experimental study on high pressure hydrogen switches is taken under pressure of 4∼13MPa and electrode gap spacing of 0.4∼1.2mm.The switch is pulse charged to more than 200kV in less than 2ns. Fast pulses with risetime less than 200ps and width less than 360ps are obtained from the output of the switches. The average breadown electric field strength is in 2∼6MV/cm. Relations between U∼d, U∼p, E∼d, and ρτ∼E/p of the H2 gaps are given and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: Phenomena of incomplete ferroelectric surface discharge
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The operation of ferroelectric plasma sources under the application of driving pulses with different amplitudes (4-40 kV) was studied. It was found that the dense plasma formation during the fast fall (a few tens of nanoseconds) of the driving pulse is accompanied by the generation of a highly diverging ~180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> neutral flow with velocity ~7·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>cm/s and charged micro-particles, in addition to the electron/ion flows studied in earlier research. It was shown that the velocity and intensity of the generated neutral flow remained the same for different parameters of the driving pulse. A model for the neutrals and micro-particles emission based on Coulomb micro-explosions of ferroelectric ceramics is suggested. The application of ferroelectric plasma source as a promising micro-thruster is discussed as well.

articleTitle: Analysis of complex cathode material emission characters
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Based on the study of explosive emission, the dielectric enhanced electric-field emission model is brought forward, and the metal-dielectric complex cathode material is manufactured. Based on the investigation of surface-flashover explosive emission, the graphite-carbon fiber complex cathode is manufactured too. Then the experiments are developed respectively, and the results show the electron emission density of these two complex cathode materials is also more than 17 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and their lifetime is excess 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> pulses.

articleTitle: Development of the prototype module of the 6MV/10MA Z-pinch test stand
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In order to study the physics of fast Z-pinches and research the key issues of pulse power technology, a 10MA/6MV z-pinch primary test stand (PTS) composed of 24 modules will be built in IFP. The prototype module adopted capacitive storage scheme has been built and tested. It is composed of the 6MV/300kJ Marx-generator (MG), intermediate storage capacitor (IC), laser-triggered switch (LTS), pulse forming line (PFL), water self-breakdown switch (WS), and tri-plate pulse transmission line (PTL). The measured output current of the prototype is approximate 520kA, and output voltage is approximate 2.1MV. The unique multi-stage LTS based on uniform field distribution design and multi-pin unsymmetrical WS make the prototype modules have low systemic delay jitter which is necessary for synchronization of multi-module facility. 1-δ jitter of delay of the system is less than 4ns.

articleTitle: Analysis of the PTS vacuum insulator stack
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The paper discussed the relationship between the structure of VIS, especially the thickness of single insulator ring, and working performances of VIS. Utilized combined analysis method with circuit simulation, MFI criterion calculation and flashover probability analysis, obtained the effects of MFI on effective pulse width t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> and on flashover probability F(t) of whole stack. The t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> will decrease and the curve of F(t) will move rightward if MFI criterion is considered. The calculation results of flashover probability on ±20 percent change of thickness of single ring are given. The curve of F(t) will move leftward if the thickness of level D decrease 20 percent. So there is possibility of compact design of the PTS VIS, in other words, the original designed VIS can working on higher voltage with same flashover probability level. In designing of z-pinch device with higher current, the MFI criterion must be considered to increase the vacuum-insulator power flow density.

articleTitle: A low guiding-magnetic-field high power millimeter-wave generator operated in the TM01 mode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: An improved high power millimeter wave generator was presented in this paper. It mainly consists of two sections of slow-wave structure (SWS) separated by the drift tube and an output cavity, and it can be operated at a relatively low magnetic field. Its working process is investigated by means of theoretical analysis and PIC simulation, and the results agree well with each other. After optimization, the guiding magnetic field can be lowered greatly as its output power and efficiency be increased. A typical simulation result is that, at the beam parameters of 600 keV and 5.1 kA, and magnetic field of 0.8T, an 8mm microwave with output power near 1GW is generated, the power conversion efficiency is over 25%, and the microwave mode is TM01 mode.

articleTitle: Dual output pulses generator based on a new type of Blumlein pulse forming line
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A novel scheme of dual output pulses generator based on a new type of Blumlein pulse forming line (PFL) is proposed. Compared with conventional Blumlein PFL, the main switch is moved to the middle of Blumlein PFL,when the main switch closes, a wave process starts in the PFL and a rectangle pulse is produced on each end of the PFL. Dual output pulses with power of 2×1GW are achieved from the new type of dual output Blumlein PFL, the dual output pulses have peak voltage of 230kV and the half amplitude width of 5ns.

articleTitle: Laser-induced breakdown experiment in nitrogen
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The characteristics of laser-induced breakdown in nitrogen at a wavelength of 1064nm were investigated with a 10-ns pulsed laser generator. The threshold field of nitrogen decreases as the pressure increases, and the experimental threshold intensities at the lower pressure were in good agreement with experimental values measured by Striker and Parker in 1982. The delay and jitter decreases while increasing the laser energy or the ratio self-breakdown voltage. Increasing gap field can accelerate the closing rate of switch. Under the conditions of average gap field 35kV/cm, ratio of laser focal length to gap length 0.065 and laser-induced energy a little greater than threshold intensities, experimental results of 25-ns delay and 20-ns jitter of switch were approached. Thus experimental results indicated that, using laser-induced breakdown switch, multi-module high power pulse devices could produce sequential pulses with inter-pulse delays of tens nanosecond.

articleTitle: Dynamics of cathode plasma speed in planar diode with explosive emission cathode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The research results of speed dynamics of explosive emission plasma expansion in the planar diode with the cathodes made of graphite and carbon fiber, of copper (solid and multi-edged) and with the multi-edged tungsten cathode are presented in the article. The plasma speed was determined by the volt-ampere characteristics of the diode with the time resolution of 0.2 ns. The experiments have been performed at the electron accelerator TEU-500 (350-450 kV, 100 ns, and 10 kA) in the matching mode of diode impedance and output resistance of nanosecond voltage generator. It was found out when the plasma formation at the cathode is completed and till the pulse ends the plasma speed is constant and equals 2±0.5 cm/μs for graphite and carbon fiber cathode, 3±0.5 cm/μs for tungsten cathode, 4±0.5 cm/μs for cathode made of copper. It is shown that the spread of explosive emission plasma is the principal tool determining its speed during the electron beam generation. The influence of the negative-charged layer by the cathode plasma surface (virtual cathode) on the additional acceleration of ions is insignificant and does not exceed 0.2-0.3 cm/μs.

articleTitle: Design of a two stage Magnetic Pulse Compression system
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A magnetic pulse compression topology is presented which does not contain external remagnetization circuits that are commonly used in magnetic compressors. Principle of operation of the compressor is described. A two stage compression system is designed based on the new MPC topology. To understand the magnetic switch operation in great detail and to model the performance of magnetic switches, a Pspice model of the Magnetic Pulse Compression (MPC) system is designed. Circuit analysis of compressor and charging system accounting for nonlinear processes in magnetic switches is discussed. Simulation and experiment results illustrated that in order to realize the desired pulse, 1μs and ~200ns magnetization period would be required for MS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and MS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, respectively. Two compression stages suffice to form 45kV, ~70ns pulses across a 207Ω resistive load.

articleTitle: Laser trigger system for multi-module facility
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The laser trigger system for multi-module was built and applied in the single module high power pulse device. The fourth harmonic (λ:266 nm) Q-switched Nd:YAG laser was used to trigger the 5 MV multi-gap multi-channel laser triggering switch. Three lasers were tested together. The experiment results show that maximum deviation (Max-Dev) and standard deviation (StDev) of jitter time of one laser is ±1.5 ns and 0.3 ns. The maximum jitter is lower than ± 2.5 ns between any two lasers.

articleTitle: X-ray emission of relativistic nonquasineutral current structures (nonthermal model of “hot spot”)
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The experiments with Z-pinches show the appearance of “hot sports”, where neutrons and x-ray emission are produced [1,2]. In the first stage of the hot-spot evolution the x-ray hardness reaches the values up to 10-12 keV, and in the second more long stage the x-ray hardness can reach the values up to 100 keV and even much higher. If the x-ray hardness in the first stage of the Z-pinch evolution can be explained by the plasma temperature, then in the second stage of the Z-pinch evolution the x-ray hardness, with the quantum energy about 100 keV and more, hardly can be explained in this manner. Therefore, some another mechanisms of the x-ray emission should be drawn. Up to now, there are various mechanisms of the generation of the x-ray emission with such a high x-ray hardness had been proposed: the forming of non-Maxwell electron distribution functions, a rapid increase of the Z-pinch resistance and the subsequent increase of the Z-pinch voltage, the generation of relativistic electron beams and maybe some others. The suggested theory includes in some sense all the enumerated features in the framework of the model, based on the violation of the plasma quasineutrality condition connected with Hall effect [3,4]. This results in the generation of the current filaments with a very high potential difference across the filament. In addition, the electron current filaments are considered at the stage when the time of their evolution is smaller than the characteristic skin time. In this case, the total filament current must be equal to zero, so that the direct current along the filament axis must be accompanied by the return current at the periphery of the filament [5]. The intercurrent repulsion results in the increase of the electron density at the axis of the inner current, where the electron velocity has a maximum value which corresponds to a high value of the transverse potential difference. One must stress that according to the recent measurements the filament currents represent only a small part of the Z-pinch current.

articleTitle: Prospects of pulsed high-current dischargein nitrogen-filled-capillary for lasing at 13.4 nm
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The recombination pumping scheme requires hot dense plasma with abundance of nuclei of active atoms (nitrogen in our case). Then this plasma has to be efficiently cooled to create at recombination of nuclei to hydrogen-like ions and their de-excitation a population inversion on Balmer-alpha transition. Such conditions can be achieved in a capillary discharge that heats plasma during compression (pinching), and cools it during expansion. The time curve (registered by vacuum photodiode) as well as the spectral composition (registered by McPherson 1 m grazing incidence spectrograph) of axially emitted EUV radiation of the pulse, high-current capillary discharge in nitrogen are investigated. It turned out that despite the pinching time is close to its optimum, the pinching process is not yet efficient enough to heat the plasma to temperature at which an abundance of nitrogen nuclei is created.

articleTitle: Studies of a novel low-impedance transit time radiation oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A novel foilless L-band low-impedance transit-time radiation oscillator was designed. Such an oscillator with coaxial structure has the advantages of low extra magnetic field, quick saturation time, and expected repetitive operation. As indicated by PIC simulations, the average power of output microwave is over 5.0GW at the main frequency of 1.583GHz with the input diode voltage of 600kV, the input diode current of 36.0kA, and the extra magnetic field of 0.45 tesla. Based on the above simulation result, the beam-wave conversion efficiency is about 22.0%, and much better than that of a high-impedance transit-time radiation oscillator with the same input voltage.

articleTitle: Resistance-voltage-dividing load used for testing and measurement in pulsed power experiments
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The resistive load is frequently used in pulsed power experiments. It has stable resistance, simple structure, and can be used repetitively in high power conditions. The resistance-voltage-dividing load introduced in this paper is a resistive load made in the form of resistance divider, thus it can be used for both device test and voltage measurement.

articleTitle: Radiographic paraxial diode experiments on RITS-6
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Intense electron beam-driven diodes are being developed for flash x-ray radiography at 7.5 - 12 MV on the RITS-6 accelerator at Sandia National Laboratories. One of several diodes under investigation is the paraxial diode in which a 40-kA electron beam is formed in vacuum, propagated through a thin anode foil, and focused inside a gas-filled transport cell onto a high-atomic-number target to generate x-rays. Two key objectives are to produce a small spot size, <;5 mm, and high forward-directed dose, >;600 R@1m. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations have shown that the primary limitation in spot size is the finite decay of the plasma return current which causes the beam focal position to sweep axially during the pulse, hence leading to an increased time-integrated spot size [1]. Recently obtained time-resolved measurements of the spot size which support this hypothesis are reported. Interpretation of these results was aided by PIC simulations in which additional physical processes were included, such as stimulated ion emission from the foil and increasing area of cathode emission [2]. Other outstanding issues for the paraxial diode on RITS-6 are also presented which include electron power-flow coupling to the diode, cavity modes which may affect focusing, and gas-breakdown physics models. Measurements of dose, dose rate, time-integrated (and time-resolved) spot size, and current are reported from experimental results primarily at 7.5 MV. Time-resolved images of the cathode emission are also presented.

articleTitle: Acceleration of macroscopic particle to hypervelocity by high intensity beams
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Hypervelocity (~1000 km/s) impact of a macroscopic particle (macron) has profound influences in high energy density physics (HEDP) and impact fusion studies. As the charge-mass ratio of macrons are too low, the length of a electrostatic accelerator can reach hundreds to thousands of kilometers, rendering hypervelocity impact impractical. To reduce the accelerator length, a much higher electric field than what the most powerful klystrons can provide is desired. One of the very few choices is the high intensity charged particle beam “blowing-pipe” scheme. In this scheme, a high intensity (~ 1 kA), medium energy (1 ~ 5 MV), long pulse (~ 1 ms) positively charged ion beam shots to a heavily charged, millimeter size macron, to create a local high strength electric field (~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> V/m), accelerating the macron. In this paper, we will present a possible approach, and the physics and challenges involved.

articleTitle: Formation of nanosized particles of silicon carbide and diamonds in surface layer of silicon target during short-pulsed implantation of carbon ions
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In the paper the study results of silicon carbide and diamond nanosized particle synthesis during short-pulsed implantation of carbon ions and protons into the silicon target are presented. The experiments have been performed at the source of high-power pulsed ion beams “TEMP” based on the magnetically isolated diode with B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> field. The beam parameters are the following: ion energy is 300 keV, pulse duration is 80 ns, beam contains ions of carbon and protons, ion current density is 30 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The plates of monocrystal silicon were used as target. After consequent action of more than 100 pulses the formation of nanosized particles SiC and nanodiamonds were observed in the surface layer of silicon. The average sizes of coherent scattering area of SiC particles and nanodiamonds were 12-16 and 8-9 nm, correspondently.

articleTitle: Synchronization of laser pulse and voltage pulse in laser-triggered surface flashover
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: With the aim of studying the characteristics of laser-triggered surface flashover in voltage pulse, synchronization problem of laser pulse and voltage pulse should be solved. Of the laser-triggered surface flashover facilities, a high precision laser trigger system is built up. A single/double harmonic, with wavelength λ of 1064/532 nm, Q-switched Nd:YAG laser is used to trigger the surface flashover. The synchronization problem is solved using a self-made digital delay/pulse generator. The delay time and jitter of Marx's trigger input and output, Marx's trigger output and Marx's output, laser input and output are respectively measured. Based on the result of the delay time and the timing sequence of the laser triggering system, digital delay/pulse generator controls Marx's trigger and the Xe lamp of laser, and the Q-switch of laser is controlled by the Marx's output. The synchronization of laser pulse and voltage pulse is obtained through adjusting the channel delay time of digital delay/pulse generator.

articleTitle: The restoration research of the burst double-pulses linear induction accelerator cell
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A linear induction accelerator (LIA) cell includes the pulse power system, the cavity and the reset system. A double-pulse cavity needs double magnetic cores contrast to a single-pulse one, so more power is required to restore those cores before the exciting pulses come. Analysis and experiments have been done to prove that, by the method of cable delay, Marx + Blumlein Pulse Forming Line (PFL) pulse power system can generate burst double-pulses output and provide enough pre-pulse to restore the magnetic cores of a double-pulse cavity before the double-pulse generation.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the microhollow cathode discharge characteristics
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a numerical simulation model was developed to simulate the helium plasma in a cylindrical hollow cathode based on a three-dimensional, time-dependent and self-consistent fluid model. Accurate solution through the continuity equations, electron energy balance equation and continuity equations with reasonable boundary conditions to get the discharge characteristics which are very important to understand the phenomena of microhollow cathode discharge. The discussions will be helpful for the design of commercial discharge structure.

articleTitle: Output rise-time estimation for high-power pulse generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Because of the difficulty of the direct measurements of the output voltage or current, a feasible approach is proposed to estimate the output parameters of the high-power pulse generator, which is based on the numerical calculation and the radiating measurement. The near-fields radiated from the biconical antenna are measured firstly, which is just excited by the pulser. Then the source functions are modeled according to the magnetic-field testing data. Finally the electromagnetic field is computed by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and compared with the testing results to validate the accuracy and reliability of the approach. The complete procedure is illustrated by the estimation of the rise-time of the output pulse.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiments on transportation of HPIB
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The experiments and numerical Simulation of HPIB (high power ion beams) transportation are presented. The transportation of HPIB in different transporting conditions and distances was studied. The influence of neutralization on the radius of beam and the uniformity of the current distribution was analyzed. The simulation code HPIBTran was programmed to calculate the waveforms of HPIB traveled to different distances. Being neutralized, the HPIB can be transported to a distance above 80cm.

articleTitle: Electrical explosion of single wire by pulsed high current
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This presents a collection of slides covering the following topics: electrical explosion of single wire; early discharge phase of wire arrays; Z-pinch; X-pinch; opening switch; production of nanopowders; and the 5 stages of wire explosion which include (i) solid heating, (ii) melting at constant temperature, (iii) liquid heating, (iv) evaporation at constant temperature, and (v) plasma formation.

articleTitle: Surface modification of TiC-NiCrAl hard alloy by pulse electron beam
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The paper presents the results of studies on the phase composition and defect substructure of a TiC-NiCrAl hard alloy treated by pulsed electron beam. The mechanisms of the evolution of the phase composition and of the defect structure of TiC crystallites and binding material responsible for the exploitation properties of the cermet were determined.

articleTitle: Primary study on a pulse trigger with laser triggered gas switch
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In pulse power system(PPS), pulse trigger is used for triggering Marx and switches of Blumlein lines. High performance pulse trigger can improve the performance and stability of the PPS. Pluse trigger with laser triggered gas switch(LTGS) has many advantages compared to electric pulse triggering mode. This paper reported the design and experimental results of pulse trigger with LTGS, with a quadruole Nd:YAG laser source.

articleTitle: Design of a transition section for 94GHz gyrotron oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Based on the general theory of mode coupling and principle of the mode converter with cosinusoidal profile, we design a transition section for 94GHz gyrotron oscillator. Numerical calculation and three-dimension electromagnetic simulation for the suggested transition section are made. The results show that the 94GHz-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-mode transition section has transmission efficiency 98.8% and low reflection below −40db within a wide bandwidth 4GHz. It is a timesaving method to design a transition section with the profile by our design.

articleTitle: Sharp electron density for laser wakefield accelerator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The electron densities of plasma channels are studied for the electron injection in laser wakefield acceleration and the effect of the finite transition scale length is studied using one-dimensional particle in cell code. The simulation indicates that the density transition scale length must be less than 2 µm for the electron injection. The density transition scale lengths were measured by an interferometer at different times. The feasible electron density structure was formed 1.2 ns after laser pulse.

articleTitle: Composite material vacuum insulator for large pulsed power facility
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: To increase the lifetime of vacuum insulators in pulsed power facility, composite material vacuum insulators have been studied in our lab. This new composite material vacuum insulators will be used in lager pulsed power facility. The composite insulators consist of a base material of epoxy and coating material of epoxy composite. The base insulators withstand the shock environment while the high voltage forced and water switch closed. Epoxy composite surface coating work in vacuum environment and develop to minimize the dendrite damage caused by the high pulse voltage and high energy electron environment. This paper will introduce the characteristic of coating materials and composite material vacuum insulator.

articleTitle: Compact repetitive Pulsed E-field Generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Provided with the advantages of long life time and high-repetition frequency, the pulsed power generator based on the Semiconductor Open Switch (SOS) has a promised prospect in the civil application. Compact repetitive Pulse E-field Generator is developed for the research of bio-effect. The generator is comprised of two parts: the pulse generator SPG50 and the parallel-plate transmission lines. The pulse generator is based on SOS and designed to deliver high voltage pulses to transmission lines. The pulsed E-field which is formed in transmission lines could be used for bio-effect. The generator can be operated on two modes; a Emax=104kV/m,FWHM=89ns,trise=40ns,repetition frequency 100Hz; b Emax=86kV/m, FWHM=15ns, trise<6ns,repetition frequency 1Hz.

articleTitle: The design and optimization of a C-band integrated mode converter and horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Research on a novel type of C-band high-power microwave mode-transducing antenna is reported. Firstly, the fundamental theory related with the designing is analyzed. Moreover, high power microwave coaxial fin inserted mode-transducing antenna for 6.2GHz is designed. The TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode is converted into TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> through coaxial fin converter. Integrating the fin-inserted mode converter and a novel horn into one structure, the mode-transducing antenna make TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode microwave radiate directly. The calculated results show that it produces a gain of 19.8dB at 6.2GHz, the maximum radiation is on the axis, and in the range of 5.95∼6.35GHz, the VSWR is below 1.5. The measured radiation patterns of the mode converter agree well with the simulated results, which indicate that the simulated results are valid.

articleTitle: Research activities on HPM at UESTC
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Presents a collection of slides covering the following topics: power sources; high power microwave sources; accelerators; gyrotron; and PIC code-CHIPIC.

articleTitle: Experimental study of semi-insulating GaAs photoconductive semiconductor switch
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A single photoconductive semiconductor switch with electrode gap of 18mm was fabricated from semi-insulating GaAs, of which the most notable defect was EL2. Photoconductivity tests were performed using 1064nm wavelength laser pulse. The PCSS began to work in the nonlinear mode at 10kV with the laser energy of 10.6mJ. The highest photocurrent tested for 11.4mJ optical excitation at the bias voltage of 20.5kV was ~2kA. A resistance of 20.7Ω was in series with the PCSS to limit the loop current because the max current Rogowski coil can measure was 2kA. Hold-off voltage tests were performed. The PCSS failed at a bias voltage of 32kV because of surface flashover.

articleTitle: Research of GaAs target erosion factor under influence of pulsed power ion beam
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In the article the results of research on the coefficient of target erosion made of GaAs at the influence of high-power pulsed ion beam are presented. In the experiments the source of high-power ion beams was used. The beam parameters are the following: ion energy is 250 keV, current density at the target is up to 250 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, pulse duration is 80 ns. The coefficient of target erosion and its dependence on the number of subsequent pulses were changed. The increase of surface roughness (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>) parameter at the increase of number of subsequent current beam pulses and the formation of regular structure of surface relief at the pulse number of 20–40 were noticed.

articleTitle: A magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator working at HEM11 mode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A novel magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator (MILO) which takes HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode as its main interaction mode is put forward for the first time in this paper. The excitation of HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode is made possible by carefully adjusting the structure parameters of each resonant cavity. The high frequency characteristics are analyzed. The special feature of such a device is that, in the slow-wave-structure (SWS) region, the interaction mode is HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode which is a TM-like one that could interact with electron beams effectively; and in the coaxial output region, the microwave mode is TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode which has a favorable field density pattern to be directly radiated. An experiment is carried out on the HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode MILO and the detailed experiment results are discussed in this paper. Employing an electron beam of about 480 kV and 39 kA, HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode MILO generates a high power microwave output of about 1.2 GW with 40 ns pulse duration at 1.98 GHz. The power conversion efficiency is about 6.5% and the generated microwave mode is TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode.

articleTitle: Study of magnetically isolated diode with dielectric anode at repetitive rate operation mode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: High-power ion beams (HPIB) find a wide application for the modification of construction material surfaces and for the deposition of metal and semi-conductive films [1]. High effectiveness of these technologies stimulates the study of magnetically isolated diodes (MID). The diodes with radial magnetic field (Br-field) possess a row of advantages [2, 3]. The important aspect of practical application of MID is the increase of MID pulse repetition rate. To create plasma on the anode, basically, two approaches are used. The first one is pulsed gas introduction in area of the anode with its subsequent ionization [4]. The second one is plasma formation on the surface of dielectric filling on the anode [5]. The increase of diode operation frequency is related to the pressure alteration in the working chamber and stability of MID parameters at that. Earlier [6] we reached a rather high life time of MID operation with dielectric anode without a significant degradation of anode coating after 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> pulses. In these studies MID with ballistic focusing and passive plasma source was used.

articleTitle: Compact repetitive PFN-LTD pulse-power generator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A new compact repetitive pulse-power generator which is based on PFN-LTD has been proposed. Prior to firing the switches, the PFN is charged in parallel directly by a high voltage power supply. The driving voltage pulses which are provided by the PFN, are set up by the linear transformer and drive the load directly without further pulse compression. This new pulse-power generator uses newly developed pulse forming module which can form low impedance and pulse width of several hundreds ns pulse easily. The experimental results indicate that the rise time of the high voltage pulse which is generated by the Blumlein pulse forming module is less than 40ns and the pulse width is about 230ns when the matching load is 2.5Ω. The charging voltage of the Blumlein pulse forming module is 6kV. A single stage PFN-LTD prototype has also been experimentally demonstrated with the rise time of the output voltage pulse about 50ns and the pulse width about 220ns under the matching load 2.5Ω. The charging voltage of the pulse forming module is 20kV. This new PFN-LTD direct driver will provide the capability to build compact repetitive pulse-power generator.

articleTitle: The optimal coupling calculation between waveguide and input cavity in relativistic klystron amplifier
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In the relativistic klystron amplifier (RKA), a large coupling hole between input cavity and waveguide port is needed for external power feeding. The optimal coupling factor is derived and a numerical method for calculating the optimal coupling factor is presented. Because of the beam loading effect of intense relativistic electron beam, the optimal coupling coefficient will be much greater than 1, which depends on the effective shunt impendence and beam current. The results indicate that the effective impendence of the cavity is much less than that of the common accelerator cavity and it reduces as the electron initial energy increases. An optimal coupling factor for the washers/rods loaded wide-gap cavity is obtained according to the effective shunt impedance and beam current.

articleTitle: Experimental studies of a Ka-band gyroklystron amplifier
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The experimental results of a four-cavity Ka-band gyroklystron amplifier operating in TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode at the fundamental of the cyclotron frequency are presented. The gyroklystron has produced 260 KW peak output power, saturated gains of 38 dB and 35% efficiency with 68 KV, 11 A annular electron beams. The full width half maximum (FWHM) bandwidth is greater than 300MHz. The amplifier is zero drive stable. Experimental results are found to be in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Simultaneous generation and transport of two microsecond sheet REBs in application to multichannel FEM
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Experimental and theoretical investigations on simultaneous generation and transport of two microsecond E-beams with the electron energy 0.8MeV, beam currents up to 3kA at a high current density ~1-1.5kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are described in the paper. Peculiarities of using such beams for a generation of mm and submm radiation in free electron maser are discussed. Parameters of the beams suitable for these applications are experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Repetition rate operation of an improved magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In order to investigate the performances of repetition rate (rep-rate) operation of an improved magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator (MILO), a series of experiments are carried out on the improved MILO device, which is driven by a 40 Ω, 50 ns rep-rate pulser: TORCH-01. Polymer velvet and graphite cathodes are tested respectively in the experiments, whose diameters and lengths are the same. The results of experimental comparison between them are presented in the paper. Both cathodes are tested at electric field strengths of about 300kV/cm. The applied voltage has 60 ns duration with a rise time of 10 ns. This paper focuses on the performance of the voltage and current characteristics, the shot-to-shot reproducibility, the pressure evolution of the diode, and the lifetime of the cathodes, not upon the radiated microwave power. The experimental results show that the graphite cathode is superior to the velvet cathode in the lifetime and the shot-to-shot reproducibility during the rep-rate operation, and it is a promising cathode for the MILO device under the rep-rate conditions.

articleTitle: Measuring intense electron beam centroid position using B-dot monitors
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Azimuthal arrays of B-dot loops are often used to measure the time-resolved beam centroid position of a pulsed, intense electron beam propagating in a metallic tube. This paper describes the designing principle, parameters and calibration of a B-dot. The preliminary experimental results in a liner induction accelerator are given.

articleTitle: GIT-4 experiments with plasma opening switch of RFNC-VNIITF design
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This report presents the experiments results carried out on the GIT-4 installation with the plasma opening switch designed in RFNC-VNIITF. Flashboards type plasma source is used for plasma injection in the switch. By the switch opening, the stored energy is transferred to the inductive load, or to the electron diode. By the conduction switch current ~1 MA, the load voltage reaches ~1 MV. The energy, dissipated in the diode with the impedance ~3 Ohm, reaches ~100 kJ. In this report, it is also discussed diode operation variations at the accelerating gap decreasing.

articleTitle: Laser differential interferometer for diagnostics of gas-puff Z-pinch
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Laser shearing interferometer (LSI) is suitable for measuring plasma density profile on condition that the spatial frequency shift of the interference fringes induced by the plasma is less than the spatial-carrier frequency of the fringes. When it is applied to diagnostics of plasmas with very large density gradient and divergence, such as current sheath produced by Z-pinch, the fringes pattern obtained in the experiment seldom meets the requirement. A new type of laser differential interferometer has been developed on the base of a cyclic LSI. By placing a ring interferometer between the two lenses of a four-focus imaging system, the interferometer has the ability to change the ratio of frequency shift to carrier frequency arbitrarily, and thus it is useful for the diagnostics of plasma with large density gradient and divergence. The principle of the four-focus differential interferometer was illustrated. Gas-puff experiments were conducted on the Yang accelerator. The interferograms of the imploding current sheath were obtained and the fringes in the sheath were distinguishable and countable. The electron density profiles and the current sheath shape were calculated from the interferograms.

articleTitle: 240keV double-pulse LIA device
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A small linear induction electron accelerator has been developed to explore the technology of generate intense electron beams in megahertz burst rate. A train of two 240keV, 1.2A electron beams was obtained in the accelerator export. Each beam has a full width at half maximum of 80ns, with rise time of 30ns, and the duration time between two beams can be adjusted easily but not less than 300ns. This paper describes the physics design, development and experimental results of the device. The key technology is analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamics of the current distribution in a discharge of the PF-3 plasma focus facility
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Results are presented from studies of the dynamics of the plasma current sheath and current distribution in the PF-3 facility, one of the largest plasma focus machines in the world, at input energies of W = 300-500 kJ and discharge currents of I ~ 2 MA, with the chamber being stationary filled with the working gas. The current sheath parameters were measured with absolutely calibrated magnetic probes installed at different distances from the system axis and at different heights above the anode plane. The possibility is demonstrated of the formation of closed current loops due to the development of shunting breakdowns in the insulator region. The maximum residual plasma density at which the electrode gap remains magnetically self-insulated is estimated.

articleTitle: Towards a self-consistent LSP model of an electron beam diode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The Large Scale Plasma (LSP) simulation tool [1] was used to investigate two different methods of modelling electron beam impact induced anode plasmas in a diode load connected to a high voltage pulsed power machine. This involved emulating an experimental study performed by researchers at the Sandia National Laboratory [2]. Both models were based on prior knowledge of the diode current and so are not fully predictive. Self-consistency, however, was evaluated by comparing results from numerical probes simulating Faraday cups, proton count monitors and a thermocouple array against experimental data. Each model assumed that protons were the predominant ion species affecting diode impedance. Of the two modelling methods that were evaluated, a temperature activated space-charge limited proton emission model proved to be the best performer. Results from a small parameter study showed that an anode surface temperature rise of 600 °C had the best agreement with experiment.

articleTitle: An inward-emitting magnetically insulated line oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) can generate microwave of GW-class without external magnetic field. The main disadvantage of the device is that part of the input power is used to maintain the insulating magnetic field, which limits the power conversion efficiency significantly. In order to increase the power conversion efficiency, a novel MILO with an inward-emitting cathode is presented. Compared with the typical outward-emitting MILO where the magnetic field is provided by the load current, the electron beam in the inward-emitting MILO is collected at a specially designed inner conductor, and the returning spoke current contributes substantially to the insulating magnetic field. The inward-emitting MILO is investigated in detail by particle-in-cell simulation and a high efficiency has been obtained.

articleTitle: Laser generation in semiconductors due to high-current picosecond electron beams
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Laser generation peculiarities in different semiconductor materials (A2B6 compositions) under the action of high-current picosecond electron beams were investigated. Current density on the sample could exceed 800 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Current pulses shorter than 300 ps FWHM were of special interest. The estimation of the current threshold densities that cause laser generation under such short pulses was given. Laser generation (line widths ~ 7 - 10 nm) in visible range on different samples (ZnSe, ZnCdS, CdS, CdS-CdSe) was obtained. The maximum pulse power of laser radiation exceeded 1000 W.

articleTitle: Runaway electron beam formation in coaxial gas-filled diode
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The formation of the runaway electron beam in the coaxial gas-filled diodes was studied by computer simulation with PIC codes KARAT and OOPIC Pro. The runaway electron current dependence of pressure for the different diode schemes was obtained. It has been shown that the runaway electron is generated mostly in cathode region. The emission process affect to the current and duration of the runaway electron pulse was studied.

articleTitle: STARFISH 1 - Towards a compact 1MA pulsed power generator for z-pinch applications
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The design and construction of STARFISH, a series of compact compact pulsed power generators to drive advanced z-pinch experiments, for applications such soft X-ray generation and as a high density plasma diagnostic, is being developed in Oxford. The design for these machines is based on the use of many very low impedance distributed pulse forming lines (PFLs) or discrete pulse forming networks (PFNs), connected in parallel, DC charged and switched simultaneously on to a load which may be a wire or laser pre-ionised channel. This generator avoids the use of very high voltage Marx generators, liquid insulated pulse forming lines and MITLs that are usually used in machines driving large z-pinch experiments. Consequently the generator is far more compact than conventional designs and should be operable at much higher repetition rates if laser pre-ionisation is used. The idea is to build a series of generators that can be operated routinely on a day-to-day basis, with pulse characteristics that can be “tailor-made” for specific loads, and be both efficient and reliable.

articleTitle: Effects of output peaking capacitor on underwater streamer propagation
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of the output peaking capacitor on the underwater streamer propagation are reported. A copper needle with 0.43 mm in diameter was used as a high voltage electrode, and an Aluminium plate was connected to ground with a 2cm gap from needle tip. Pulsed streamer propagation in tap water with conductivity of 225μS/cm was observed using an intensified charge-coupled display (ICCD) camera with a high-speed gate. An output peaking capacitor was connected in parallel with point-to-plate electrodes. From the results, it was observed that the streamer discharges formed thick and small channels in the case of without a peaking capacitor. Thin and average distribution channels were observed in the case of using a peaking capacitor.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of the Z-pinch loads on the PTS facility
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a method for designing and optimizing the wire-array loads used on the PTS facility is presented. Both ZP-0D program of a shell model and MARED-1D code of a MHD model are used for the simulation. By comparing results from each model, the characteristics of the Z-pinch implosion plasma driven by the PTS facility are investigated, and the load parameters are optimized. It is found that, a 15nH concentrator inductance is efficient for PTS facility to work at load currents up to 10MA. The optimized tungsten wire-array load is able to produce x-ray radiation at peak power up to 100TW and a best efficiency of conversion from the wall-plug of about 10%. By further investigation and comparison with experiment datum, it is supposed that PTS facility will has similar x-ray radiation productivity with Saturn facility operating at a long-pulse mode.

articleTitle: High power microwave generation by a novel vircator with coaxial waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A new configuration of a vircator is put forward for high power microwave generation. In this configuration, a coaxial waveguide and a hollow electric beam are used to enhance the beam-wave interaction and reduce the energy divergence of the injected electric beam in order to improve the microwave efficiency. A one-dimensional analytical model is used to describe the steady-state behavior of the electron beam and the virtual cathode, from which the space-charged limited current and the output microwave power are obtained. The preliminary 2.5-D particle-in-cell simulations using KARAT are carried out with typical electron-beam parameters of 550keV and 60kA, where pulsed microwave of 1.8GW in average power and 5.0GHz in the TM02 mode is obtained. The power efficiency from the electron beam to microwaves is 4.8%.

articleTitle: Diamagnetic loop diagnoses emittance of intense pulse beam
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The technology of diamagnetic loop diagnosing intense pulse beam is on-line diagnostics. The technology can diagnoses beam emittance and obliquity on-line cooperating with other technology such as three gradient method. In this paper, we introduce theory of diamagnetic loop, design and calibrate diamagnetic loop device. And we diagnose Dragon- I accelerator electron beams radius and emittance. By the DML, average beam radius in the flat of pulse in the !2th accelerator cavity is 17.25mm, which are accordant with the result of CR measuring. Emittance at the exit of accelerator is 2480 π ·mm· mrad.

articleTitle: Ion acceleration by moving virtual cathode during the electron beam “compressed” state collapse
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Theoretical and numerical studies of the collective acceleration of positively charged ions by a moving virtual cathode in a cylindrical two-section transport system were conducted. It is shown that on decay of a compressed electron beam, the mechanism of ion acceleration is more efficient than that during the formation of a compressed beam, where the virtual cathode shits toward the injection plane. For the SINUS-7 accelerator parameters under study, the output ion energy was several times greater than the injected electron energy.

articleTitle: High power and high-longevity GaAs photoconductive semiconductor switches
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A 14mm photoconductive semiconductor switch (PCSS) is excited at 20kV/400A, and the longevity is up to 350 shots. After 350 shots, the dark resistances decreases, and the biased voltage can not be increased to 20 kV again. The breakdown mechanism and the cause of the dark resistances decrease of the PCSS is analyzed based on the breakdown characteristics.

articleTitle: Initial LSP simulations of electron beam transport in gas filled drift cells and comparison with experiments performed on the eta II linear induction acceleration at LLNL
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The Pulsed Power group at AWE are using the LSP (Large-Scale-Plasma) code to support the design of X-radiographic diodes for the forthcoming facility Hydrus. Part of the design process requires validation of LSP through various experiments. The aim of the work here is to demonstrate LSP's ability to model electron beam transport through gas cells. Previous work suggests the electron beam focuses in a betatron manner where it becomes appropriate to place the high Z target of the diode at the first focus. A Cherenkov radiation foil was used to locate the position of a betatron point or waist. Resistive current monitors gave the time evolution of the net currents which control the amount of beam sweep in the ionised gas. Light from the beam generated plasma was used to highlight the envelope of the electron beam.

articleTitle: Development of nanosecond pulsed high-power amorphous cores
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Owing to high saturation flux density and high flux swing, the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">78</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf> amorphous cores are possessed of distinctive superiority relatively to ferrite, silicon iron cores, and permalloy cores in the field of short pulsed high-power technology. Depending on the type of magnetic material and manufacturing technology, magnetic cores have different properties. In this paper, design, manufacturing technology and property about nanosecond pulsed high-power Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">78</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf> amorphous cores produced by Liyuan Company are described.

articleTitle: The study of the framing technology on Z-Pinch plasma imaging diagnosticate
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The study of Z-Pinch plasma dynamics is base on space and time resolution diagnosticate. The article introduces that the principle and the configuration of a x-ray framing camera which is used on Z-pinch plasma dynamics process diagnosticate. The technology about anti-jamming and the frame pulse synchronization and delay was studied in experiments. The legible framing images of Z-Pinch plasma was ultimately obtained.

articleTitle: Experiment WEX - Wire explosion in water
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: A new wire explosion driver WEX (Wire EXplosion) with a laser-triggered main spark gap has been designed and built. Our motivation for building such new apparatus was testing of feasibility of amplification of spontaneous emission in soft X-ray region at shorter wavelengths (below 20 nm). One of the ways how to achieve shortening the wavelengths is amplification based on electron-collisional excitation pumping of some metal vapours. Feeding these vapours into capillary is difficult; therefore, metal vapour plasma in a capillary with liquid wall is being prepared. This paper reports on new results characterizing wire explosion in water, namely time dependences of the discharge current, and the XUV/soft X-ray radiation emitted axially by expanding and collapsing plasma channel.

articleTitle: Design of high voltage pulsed power supply using storage battery as prime power source
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces a design of high voltage pulse power supply that uses storage battery as prime power resource. This high voltage pulse power supply system can work without alternating current power supply and can be controlled by the remote control centre. Besides, some important information can be gained and displayed on the computer, such as the position, status, measured feedback of output voltage and current and so on. The purpose of the design is that the system can not only reliably work in laboratory but also outdoors. Mostly, we can use this system to drive some important high voltage equipments, such as accelerator of intense charged particle beams, explosively-driven magnetic flux compression generators and so on. To ensure the system to work reliably and stably, this paper analyzes the interference sources, interference channels, because this system may work in complicated electromagnetism condition. And some effective anti-interference measures of both hardware and software are used in the design.

articleTitle: New approaches to enhance the output power in an HMFCG
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Two approaches to enhance the output power and current of a flux trapping two staged HMFCG are proposed. Influences of these efforts on its performance is analyzed systematically by using code MFCG-IV, which is a 2D MHD code used to model the dynamic behavior of magnetic flux compression generators with helically wound coils. A series of models have been simulated and analyzed. Simulation results show that the output power of an HMFCG can be enhanced dramatically.

articleTitle: Impact of conductors accelerated by a pulsed high magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Paper is devoted to the study of impact of metallic foils accelerated by a pulsed high magnetic field. The numerical model of foil acceleration under effect of magnetic field pressure is elaborated. The facility TROB-100 was adapted and special equipment was constructed for this activity. The tool description, results of experiments on high-velocity impact of metallic foils, accelerated by a magnetic field pressure are presented in this paper. The purpose of the work is to study foils acceleration dynamics and decomposition and also to measure the dimension of products of explosion. Two metal foils were accelerated by a pulsed magnetic field up to relative velocity ~ 1-2 km/s. At the impact of the foils the directed energy is transferred to thermal energy during the time of order of sound propagation time in a metal foil. It is shown, that the foils are exploded at relative velocity of impact more than 1km/s. The size of explosion fragments is in the range of 5-100 nm.

articleTitle: The influence of high negative substrate pulse bias on bulk plasma density
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In this paper, we have used a dual Langmuir probe system to locate the edge of sheath and studied the influence of high negative pulse bias on bulk plasma density. Bulk plasma density changes greatly with and without substrate bias, but is insensitive to different non-zero substrate bias. Pulse width and frequency has greater influence on bulk plasma density, but there is not a simple linear increase between them, inflexion is observed with longer pulse width and higher frequency. We use two competitive interaction mechanisms ——ionization cross sections and the secondary electron emission to explain the phenomenon above.

articleTitle: PIC simulation of a novel microwave oscillator based on the self-modulation of annular intense relativistic electron beam
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: While an annular intensely relativistic electron beam (IREB) is going through an equi-potential resonant cavity, because of the space-charge effect, static electric field is formed in the cavity, and annular static magnetic field is formed by the IREB itself at the same time. The strong electric field and magnetic field make the electron beam oscillate continuously, which is called self-modulation. Based on this mechanism, the structural design and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of a novel microwave oscillator are given. After optimization, 1.7GW microwave output power with a dominant frequency of 4.44GHz can be obtained while a 13.5kA, 1.29MeV electron beam is injected into a 4.5cm long resonant cavity. The efficiency of this oscillator is about 10%.

articleTitle: Cost optimization of HPM systems
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: For fixed power density in the far field, what is the cost-optimum HPM system? We derive general relations for cost-optimal aperture and power. For linear dependence of capital cost on transmitter power and antenna area, minimum capital cost occurs when the cost is equally divided between antenna gain and radiated power. For non-linear power law dependence a similar simple division occurs. This is validated in cost data for many systems and is used as a rule-of-thumb in industry. Cost of pulsed cost-efficient transmitters can be estimated using these relations using current cost parameters ($/W, $/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) as a basis.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of pulse forming line (PFL) charged by capacitance through transformer considering the energy recuperation
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: According to the theory of transformer equivalent circuit, the theoretical study of PFL charged by capacitance through transformer considering the energy recuperation is presented. The analytical expression of counter-voltage of the primary capacitance is obtained when the PFL has been discharged, so the energy transferring efficiency from primary capacitance to PFL considering the energy recuperation, which depends on the parameters of the circuit is got and analyzed. There existing an optimum value of the coupling coefficient of the transformer which is not near to 1, but about 0.8–0.9 in the practical circuit, the results also show that it is very important to reduce farthest the loop resistance. These conclusions are very useful to the design of the transformer and the circuit.

articleTitle: Simulation investigation of an improved L-band ladder cathode MILO
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Optimization for L-band ladder cathode MILO based on an existing model is carried out. The efficiency is improved by changing the parameters of choke and SWS vanes. The resonant frequency and Q factor are obtained through numerical calculation of open cavity high frequency characteristics. Then a 2.5-dimensional electromagnetic PIC code is used for optimizing simulation. Employing an electron beam of 568 kV, 53.3 kA, a TEM mode high power microwave with output power of 5.5GW, frequency of 1.2GHz is obtained. The power conversion efficiency is 18.2%.

Author Keywords: high frequency analysis of open cavity

articleTitle: Long pulse high power microwave generation by coaxial vircator
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Experiment results of long pulse high power microwave (HPM) generation by coaxial vircator is proposed. The HV generator-MC55 is rebuilt to provide the diode voltage ranging from 300kV to 500kV under 10Ω diode impedance with 100ns pulse width. Long pulse coaxial vircator system is built, and a power of 570MW, S band HPM pulse with 80ns FWHA is obtained in the experiment. The relationship between pulse shortening effect and diode gap is experimentally studied, which shows that the HPM pulsed length is in direct ratio with diode gap. Under the optimized experimental configuration, no pulse shortening effect caused by the factor other than diode voltage fluctuation is observed, which is also in consistent with the PIC simulation results.

articleTitle: Investigations of cold cathode emission in gas and vacuum with picosecond resolution
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: Electron beam formation in magnetically insulated coaxial diode with tubular cold cathode and a strongly non-uniform electric field was investigated with picosecond resolution. Voltage pulses of amplitudes up to -170 kV (in a traveling wave mode) and FWHM not exceed 250 ps were applied to the cathode. Under such accelerating pulse parameters the polishing effect has a fundamental influence on the emissive characteristics. The time and amplitude parameters of electron beam injection were compared experimentally for different cathode materials with gas or vacuum insulation of accelerating gap.

articleTitle: Research of inductance period of hydrogen-oxygen mixture ignition by pulsed electron beam action
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The experimental study of inductance period of hydrogen-oxygen mixture ignition by pulsed electron beam has been performed. It is shown when the external influence is applied to the hydrogen-oxygen mixture a significant decrease of inductance period takes place. Also, it is found out that the dependence of inductance period of mixture ignition on pressure has a shape typical for chain processes that is the increase of inductance period by the ignition boundaries.

articleTitle: Secondary electron emission characteristic of nanocrystalline diamond films
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: The preparation, characterization and application of nanocrystalline diamond films have become a new “hot point” in the development of diamond films prepared by chemical vapor deposition. In this paper, we simply introduced the preparation process of nano-crystalline diamond films with MPCVD method, and the result of surface analysis. Then we designed an experiment device to measure the SEE coefficient(δ) in emission mode. A good result (δ =15) has been obtained.

articleTitle: A short dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 17th International Conference on High Power Particle Beams (BEAMS)
abstract: In order to reduce the effective area of the receiving antenna to receiving microwave power in high electric field regions, a short dipole antenna is investigated numerically and experimentally in this paper. The short dipole antenna is a variation of the conventional half-wave antenna. A 50 Ω coaxial transmission line with two symmetrical narrow slots is employed as a feeder of the short dipole antenna. The simulation results show that the general gain and the effective area of the short dipole antenna to receiving microwave power are −10.21dBi and 2.19 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> respectively.
